tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.content:
1	# Feature Specification: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `011-settings-dashboard` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-24
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard: Build the Settings screen with the evolution dashboard, and the profile and account actions that live on it. Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF09; RNF05 (section 4) for account deletion. Prototype states: 'Tela 6 — Configurações' in its four dashboard variations and 'Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta' (prototype extract, section 2.6); profile name editing, 'Sair' and 'Apagar conta'. Backend: GET /dashboard/aggregate, GET /dashboard/narrative, PATCH /account/settings, DELETE /account, POST /auth/logout. Depends on: F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements, section 2), or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-24
14	
15	- Q: What should the dashboard show for an account with more than one entry but not yet enough to fill the chart's full set of bars (e.g. 5 or 15 entries) — a state the spec's three enumerated scenarios (zero / exactly one / more than thirty) never covered? → A: Render the multi-bar chart using whatever of the ten bars the aggregate's buckets actually populate — naturally partial for a small count — and request the narrative for any count of two or more; "more than thirty" is the seed count chosen to reliably exercise a fully-populated demo chart, not a distinct functional threshold.
16	- Q: For the fixed `all` period, which can span anywhere from a few days to years of history, how should the backend's date-bucketed aggregate be mapped onto the chart's fixed ten bars? → A: Client-side, divide the account's full date range (date of the first entry through today) into ten roughly-equal time slices and sum the backend's per-date counts that fall within each slice to produce each bar's value.
17	- Q: Should the Face ID/Touch ID toggle be hidden entirely or shown-but-disabled on a device with no usable biometric capability? → A: Hidden entirely — the toggle row is omitted from Settings rather than shown in a disabled state.
18	
19	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
20	
21	### User Story 1 - Seeing your evolution dashboard (Priority: P1)
22	
23	The user opens the Settings screen and sees, at a glance, a chart of how their recorded entries have built up over time, plus a short AI-written paragraph that puts that pattern into words. Whether they have no entries yet, just one, or a long history, the screen always shows something coherent rather than breaking or looking empty by accident.
24	
25	**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF09 — without a correctly rendering chart and narrative, the feature does not exist. **Scope: aggregation and rendering only — the quality of the AI-written narrative text is never evaluated.**
26	
27	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening Settings for accounts seeded with zero, one, and more than thirty entries respectively, and confirming each renders its own distinct, non-crashing state with the correct chart and text.
28	
29	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
30	
31	1. **Given** the user has zero entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a light-gray placeholder chart icon (no chart) and the text "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui", with no AI narrative paragraph shown or requested.
32	2. **Given** the user has exactly one entry, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.", with no AI narrative paragraph attempted.
33	3. **Given** the user has more than thirty entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a multi-bar ochre chart (aggregated into the chart's fixed number of buckets) and, once it loads, an AI-written summary paragraph describing the pattern.
34	4. **Given** the chart has loaded successfully for an account with data, **When** the AI narrative call fails or times out, **Then** the chart remains visible and correct, and the narrative area shows a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message rather than staying blank or showing the empty-history copy.
35	5. **Given** the user created a new entry in another screen since Settings was last open, **When** they open Settings again, **Then** the dashboard reflects the new entry in its aggregate — recomputed fresh, not read from a stale result of the previous visit.
36	6. **Given** the user has more than one entry but not enough to populate every one of the chart's ten bars (e.g. 5 or 15 entries), **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows the same multi-bar chart and narrative behavior as the "more than thirty entries" case, just with fewer of the ten bars populated — not the single-bar "Ainda é cedo..." message and not a separate, undefined state.
37	
38	---
39	
40	### User Story 2 - Deleting your account for good (Priority: P1)
41	
42	A user who wants to leave can permanently erase their account and every piece of data tied to it, with a clear, hard-to-misclick warning first, and no way to undo it afterward.
43	
44	**Why this priority**: Required by RNF05 (LGPD hard delete) — a legal and trust-critical capability, not a convenience feature. Getting this wrong (deleting too little, deleting by accident, or appearing to delete without really doing so) is a compliance and trust failure, not just a bug.
45	
46	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "Apagar conta", confirming through the destructive dialog, and verifying the account can no longer log in and the Settings screen is left entirely (no residual session), independent of any other screen.
47	
48	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
49	
50	1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** they tap "Apagar conta", **Then** a centered confirmation dialog appears with a red title ("Apagar sua conta?"), explanatory text that the action is permanent and irreversible, a red "Apagar tudo" button, and an outline "Cancelar" button.
51	2. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Cancelar", **Then** the dialog closes, no backend call is made, and Settings is otherwise unaffected.
52	3. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Apagar tudo", **Then** the app requests the account's permanent deletion, and on success clears all local session and account state and leaves the user at the app's authentication entry point, with no "account deleted" success screen of its own.
53	4. **Given** the deletion request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the account is left intact, the user sees a clear error, and can retry — the dialog does not falsely report success.
54	
55	---
56	
57	### User Story 3 - Signing out and managing your profile (Priority: P2)
58	
59	From the same screen, the user can see their profile, rename themselves, flip the Face ID/Touch ID unlock preference on or off, and sign out — all lower-stakes, everyday actions compared to Stories 1 and 2.
60	
61	**Why this priority**: Explicitly named in the feature's scope ("the profile and account actions that live on it") but individually lower risk and lower complexity than the dashboard or account deletion.
62	
63	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by editing the display name and confirming it persists after reopening the app, flipping the biometric toggle and confirming it is saved, and tapping "Sair" and confirming the session ends.
64	
65	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
66	
67	1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** the screen loads, **Then** it shows an initials avatar (52px), the current display name and email, and the editable-name control as a pencil icon.
68	2. **Given** the user taps the pencil icon next to their name, **When** the name field becomes editable, **Then** the pencil icon becomes a check icon and the email remains read-only (not editable) throughout.
69	3. **Given** the user edits their name to a valid value (1–80 characters) and taps the check icon, **When** the save request succeeds, **Then** the field returns to display mode showing the new name, and the new name is still shown after the app is restarted.
70	4. **Given** the save request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the field stays in edit mode with the user's typed text intact, a clear error is shown, and the user can retry without re-typing.
71	5. **Given** the device supports biometrics, **When** the user flips the "Face ID/Touch ID" toggle on Settings, **Then** the app saves the new preference, and the toggle reflects the saved state (or reverts with an error if the save fails).
72	6. **Given** the user taps "Sair", **When** the sign-out request completes (or fails), **Then** the local session is cleared either way, and the user lands at the app's authentication entry point with no residual access to their data.
73	
74	---
75	
76	### Edge Cases
77	
78	- The GET /dashboard/aggregate call itself fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), independent of the narrative call: the dashboard shows a clear, non-crashing error state for the chart area (distinct from the "zero entries" empty state) with a way to retry, and no narrative is requested until the aggregate succeeds.
79	- The session expires while Settings is open (dashboard loading, name being edited, or a confirmation dialog open): the existing expired-session handling (established by F000, continued by RF07) takes over exactly as it does elsewhere; re-authenticating returns the user to Settings with the dashboard, profile, and any in-progress edit reasonably re-requested, not silently lost.
80	- The user double-taps "Apagar tudo" or "Sair" before the first request resolves: this does not fire a second concurrent delete/logout request.
81	- The device has no biometric hardware or nothing enrolled: the toggle row is hidden entirely (not shown in a disabled state), rather than letting the user "turn on" something the device cannot perform.
82	- The user submits an empty name or one over 80 characters: the save is blocked client-side with a clear validation message, no request is sent, and the field stays in edit mode.
83	- Opening Settings, viewing the dashboard, editing the profile, or opening (and cancelling) the delete-confirmation dialog does not alter any other screen's state — My Records' list/filters, chat sessions, or action plans are untouched by this unit.
84	
85	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
86	
87	### Functional Requirements
88	
89	- **FR-001**: Opening Settings MUST request `GET /dashboard/aggregate` and `GET /dashboard/narrative` as two independent calls, so that a narrative failure or delay never blocks the chart from rendering with the aggregate data it already has.
90	- **FR-002**: The dashboard MUST request and render a single, fixed period and MUST NOT present a user-facing control to switch between periods in this unit — the prototype shows no such control, and only the fixed period's acceptance scenarios (zero / one / more than thirty entries) are in scope.
91	- **FR-003**: When the aggregate for the active period contains zero entries, the dashboard MUST show the light-gray placeholder chart icon and "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui", and MUST NOT request or show the narrative.
92	- **FR-004**: When the aggregate contains exactly one entry, the dashboard MUST show a single small bar and "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.", and MUST NOT request or show the narrative.
93	- **FR-005**: When the aggregate contains two or more entries, the dashboard MUST render the multi-bar chart using whatever of the chart's ten bars the aggregate's buckets populate — naturally partial for a small count, fully populated once an account has enough history (the "more than thirty entries" scenario is the seed count chosen to reliably exercise a fully-populated chart, not a distinct functional threshold) — and MUST request the narrative, showing it once it resolves.
94	- **FR-006**: If the narrative call fails, times out, or returns an error after the chart has already rendered successfully, the dashboard MUST show a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message in the narrative's place, without affecting the already-rendered chart and without being confused with the zero-entries empty state.
95	- **FR-007**: If the aggregate call itself fails, the dashboard MUST show a clear, non-crashing, retryable error state for the chart area, distinct from the zero-entries state, and MUST NOT request the narrative until the aggregate succeeds.
96	- **FR-008**: The dashboard MUST be recomputed from a fresh backend call every time Settings is opened, never served from a result cached from a previous visit, so that an entry created elsewhere is reflected the next time Settings is opened.
97	- **FR-009**: Settings MUST display the account's initials avatar, current display name, and current email (read-only) — email MUST NOT be editable in this unit, since `PATCH /account/settings` accepts no email field and rejects attempts to change it.
98	- **FR-010**: Settings MUST let the user edit their display name through an inline pencil-to-check control; saving MUST call `PATCH /account/settings` with the new `displayName` (1–80 characters) and MUST update the locally displayed/cached name on success.
99	- **FR-011**: A client-side validation MUST block submitting an empty name or one longer than 80 characters, with no backend call made and the field left in edit mode with an inline error.
100	- **FR-012**: If the name save fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the field MUST remain in edit mode with the user's typed value intact, show a clear retryable error, and MUST NOT silently revert or discard the typed text.
101	- **FR-013**: On a device where biometrics are available, Settings MUST offer a toggle reflecting the account's current `biometricEnabled` preference and MUST let the user change it; changing it MUST call `PATCH /account/settings` with the new `biometricEnabled` value, continuing the account-settings read/write path RF03 already established for this same flag. On a device with no biometric hardware or nothing enrolled, the toggle row MUST be hidden entirely rather than shown in a disabled state.
102	- **FR-014**: If the biometric toggle save fails, the toggle MUST revert to its last-confirmed state and show a clear, retryable error, rather than appearing to succeed.
103	- **FR-015**: This unit MUST NOT build the AI persona selector ("Analítico"/"Empático"/"Socrático") or any other extension feature (requirements, section 2), even though `PATCH /account/settings` also carries a `persona` field for that extension.

# Feature Specification: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard

**Feature Branch**: `011-settings-dashboard` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-24

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard: Build the Settings screen with the evolution dashboard, and the profile and account actions that live on it. Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF09; RNF05 (section 4) for account deletion. Prototype states: 'Tela 6 — Configurações' in its four dashboard variations and 'Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta' (prototype extract, section 2.6); profile name editing, 'Sair' and 'Apagar conta'. Backend: GET /dashboard/aggregate, GET /dashboard/narrative, PATCH /account/settings, DELETE /account, POST /auth/logout. Depends on: F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements, section 2), or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-24

- Q: What should the dashboard show for an account with more than one entry but not yet enough to fill the chart's full set of bars (e.g. 5 or 15 entries) — a state the spec's three enumerated scenarios (zero / exactly one / more than thirty) never covered? → A: Render the multi-bar chart using whatever of the ten bars the aggregate's buckets actually populate — naturally partial for a small count — and request the narrative for any count of two or more; "more than thirty" is the seed count chosen to reliably exercise a fully-populated demo chart, not a distinct functional threshold.
- Q: For the fixed `all` period, which can span anywhere from a few days to years of history, how should the backend's date-bucketed aggregate be mapped onto the chart's fixed ten bars? → A: Client-side, divide the account's full date range (date of the first entry through today) into ten roughly-equal time slices and sum the backend's per-date counts that fall within each slice to produce each bar's value.
- Q: Should the Face ID/Touch ID toggle be hidden entirely or shown-but-disabled on a device with no usable biometric capability? → A: Hidden entirely — the toggle row is omitted from Settings rather than shown in a disabled state.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Seeing your evolution dashboard (Priority: P1)

The user opens the Settings screen and sees, at a glance, a chart of how their recorded entries have built up over time, plus a short AI-written paragraph that puts that pattern into words. Whether they have no entries yet, just one, or a long history, the screen always shows something coherent rather than breaking or looking empty by accident.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF09 — without a correctly rendering chart and narrative, the feature does not exist. **Scope: aggregation and rendering only — the quality of the AI-written narrative text is never evaluated.**

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening Settings for accounts seeded with zero, one, and more than thirty entries respectively, and confirming each renders its own distinct, non-crashing state with the correct chart and text.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user has zero entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a light-gray placeholder chart icon (no chart) and the text "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui", with no AI narrative paragraph shown or requested.
2. **Given** the user has exactly one entry, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.", with no AI narrative paragraph attempted.
3. **Given** the user has more than thirty entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a multi-bar ochre chart (aggregated into the chart's fixed number of buckets) and, once it loads, an AI-written summary paragraph describing the pattern.
4. **Given** the chart has loaded successfully for an account with data, **When** the AI narrative call fails or times out, **Then** the chart remains visible and correct, and the narrative area shows a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message rather than staying blank or showing the empty-history copy.
5. **Given** the user created a new entry in another screen since Settings was last open, **When** they open Settings again, **Then** the dashboard reflects the new entry in its aggregate — recomputed fresh, not read from a stale result of the previous visit.
6. **Given** the user has more than one entry but not enough to populate every one of the chart's ten bars (e.g. 5 or 15 entries), **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows the same multi-bar chart and narrative behavior as the "more than thirty entries" case, just with fewer of the ten bars populated — not the single-bar "Ainda é cedo..." message and not a separate, undefined state.

---

### User Story 2 - Deleting your account for good (Priority: P1)

A user who wants to leave can permanently erase their account and every piece of data tied to it, with a clear, hard-to-misclick warning first, and no way to undo it afterward.

**Why this priority**: Required by RNF05 (LGPD hard delete) — a legal and trust-critical capability, not a convenience feature. Getting this wrong (deleting too little, deleting by accident, or appearing to delete without really doing so) is a compliance and trust failure, not just a bug.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "Apagar conta", confirming through the destructive dialog, and verifying the account can no longer log in and the Settings screen is left entirely (no residual session), independent of any other screen.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** they tap "Apagar conta", **Then** a centered confirmation dialog appears with a red title ("Apagar sua conta?"), explanatory text that the action is permanent and irreversible, a red "Apagar tudo" button, and an outline "Cancelar" button.
2. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Cancelar", **Then** the dialog closes, no backend call is made, and Settings is otherwise unaffected.
3. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Apagar tudo", **Then** the app requests the account's permanent deletion, and on success clears all local session and account state and leaves the user at the app's authentication entry point, with no "account deleted" success screen of its own.
4. **Given** the deletion request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the account is left intact, the user sees a clear error, and can retry — the dialog does not falsely report success.

---

### User Story 3 - Signing out and managing your profile (Priority: P2)

From the same screen, the user can see their profile, rename themselves, flip the Face ID/Touch ID unlock preference on or off, and sign out — all lower-stakes, everyday actions compared to Stories 1 and 2.

**Why this priority**: Explicitly named in the feature's scope ("the profile and account actions that live on it") but individually lower risk and lower complexity than the dashboard or account deletion.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by editing the display name and confirming it persists after reopening the app, flipping the biometric toggle and confirming it is saved, and tapping "Sair" and confirming the session ends.

1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** the screen loads, **Then** it shows an initials avatar (52px), the current display name and email, and the editable-name control as a pencil icon.
2. **Given** the user taps the pencil icon next to their name, **When** the name field becomes editable, **Then** the pencil icon becomes a check icon and the email remains read-only (not editable) throughout.
3. **Given** the user edits their name to a valid value (1–80 characters) and taps the check icon, **When** the save request succeeds, **Then** the field returns to display mode showing the new name, and the new name is still shown after the app is restarted.
4. **Given** the save request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the field stays in edit mode with the user's typed text intact, a clear error is shown, and the user can retry without re-typing.
5. **Given** the device supports biometrics, **When** the user flips the "Face ID/Touch ID" toggle on Settings, **Then** the app saves the new preference, and the toggle reflects the saved state (or reverts with an error if the save fails).

# Cerne Constitution

### I. Product Source of Truth
`docs/input/` — `requirements.md`, `prototype/`, and `backend/` — is the
authoritative source for product behavior. `requirements.md` defines
functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery
order, and technical constraints; `prototype/` is the frozen visual

API, error taxonomy, screen-state map, sync-badge semantics, and fixtures.

technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under

this repository.

product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
stable.

using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to

HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
and charting — are open implementation decisions.

Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
built by different contributors or at different times.

### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
NEVER be committed.

Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
credential leakage.

### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity

spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI

checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen

```

layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules

These targets from `docs/input/requirements.md` are binding quality gates:

1	# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow
2	
3	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.
4	
5	This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Functional requirements
10	
11	### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12	Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
13	
14	**Acceptance criteria:**
15	- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
16	- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.
17	
18	### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19	Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.
22	
23	### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
24	Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
25	
26	**Acceptance criteria:**
27	- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
28	- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).
29	
30	### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
31	Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.
32	
33	**Acceptance criteria:**
34	- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
35	- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).
36	
37	### RF05 — Personal summary export
38	Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
39	
40	**Acceptance criteria:**
41	- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
42	- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
43	
44	### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45	Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46	
47	**Acceptance criteria:**
48	- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49	- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50	- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51	- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52	- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.
53	
54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.
61	
62	### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
63	A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**
64	
65	**Acceptance criteria:**
66	- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
67	- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
68	- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.
69	
70	### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
71	An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**
72	
73	**Acceptance criteria:**
74	- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
75	- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
76	- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.
77	
78	### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
79	A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.
80	
81	**Acceptance criteria:**
82	- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
83	- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
84	- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
85	- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 2. Extension features — not implemented
90	
91	They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.
92	
93	| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
94	|---|---|
95	| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
96	| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
97	| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |
98	
99	---
100	
101	## 3. Quality requirements
102	
103	| ID | Requirement | Target |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
106	| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
107	| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
108	| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |
109	
110	## 4. Other non-functional requirements
111	
112	RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).
113	
114	**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow
119	
120	### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
121	Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.
122	
123	### 5.2 Screens
124	
125	**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*
126	
127	**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*
128	
129	**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*
130	
131	**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*
132	
133	**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*
134	
135	**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*
136	
137	**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*
138	
139	**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 6. Backend endpoint inventory
144	
145	The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.
146	
147	Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.
148	
149	### 6.1 Authentication and session
150	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
151	|---|---|---|
152	| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
153	| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
154	| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
155	| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
156	| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |
157	
158	**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).
159	
160	### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
161	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
164	| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
165	| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
166	| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |
167	
168	**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.
169	
170	### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
171	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
172	|---|---|---|
173	| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
174	| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
175	| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |
176	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI (question embedding) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
177	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` — regenerates the response without duplicating the user's question; it supports "partial message visible with a failure indication, and a way to try again" in RF04 | RF04 | Voyage AI (embedding, reused from cache) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
178	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
179	| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
180	
181	### 6.4 Search
182	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
183	|---|---|---|
184	| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |
185	
186	### 6.5 Export
187	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
188	|---|---|---|
189	| `POST /export/summary` — asynchronous job | RF05 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
190	| `GET /export/:jobId/status` | RF05 | — |
191	| `GET /export/:jobId/download` | RF05 | — |
192	
193	### 6.6 Dashboard
194	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
195	|---|---|---|
196	| `GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=` — separate from the text so it does not block the chart | RF09 | — |
197	| `GET /dashboard/narrative?period=` | RF09 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
198	
199	### 6.7 Account
200	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
201	|---|---|---|
202	| `PATCH /account/settings` — includes the persona toggle (extension) | RNF05, extension | — |
203	| `DELETE /account` | RNF05 | — |

339	| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
340	| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
341	| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
342	| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |

345	| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |

361	- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

366

368	- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).

371	- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
372	- Test doubles: `mocktail`.

374	- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.

386	```

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

---

## 2. Extension features — not implemented

They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.

| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
|---|---|
| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |

---

## 3. Quality requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target |
|---|---|---|
| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |

## 4. Other non-functional requirements

RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).

**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.

---

## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow

### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

### 5.2 Screens

**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*

**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*

**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*

**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*

**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*

**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*

**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*

**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*

---

## 6. Backend endpoint inventory

The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.

Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.

### 6.1 Authentication and session
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |

**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).

### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |

**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.

### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI (question embedding) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` — regenerates the response without duplicating the user's question; it supports "partial message visible with a failure indication, and a way to try again" in RF04 | RF04 | Voyage AI (embedding, reused from cache) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |

### 6.4 Search
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |

### 6.5 Export
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /export/summary` — asynchronous job | RF05 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `GET /export/:jobId/status` | RF05 | — |
| `GET /export/:jobId/download` | RF05 | — |

### 6.6 Dashboard
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=` — separate from the text so it does not block the chart | RF09 | — |
| `GET /dashboard/narrative?period=` | RF09 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |

### 6.7 Account
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH /account/settings` — includes the persona toggle (extension) | RNF05, extension | — |
| `DELETE /account` | RNF05 | — |

---

## 7. Integrated flowchart — screens × requirements × backend

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph T0["Screen 0 — Splash"]
        direction TB
        E01["GET /auth/session"]
    end

    subgraph T01["Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault · RF03"]

    end

    subgraph T1["Screen 1 — Home (chat) · RF04, RF08, RF10"]

    end

    subgraph T2["Screen 2 — Insertion modal · RF01, RF02"]

    end

*(The amber "Action plans" subgraph marks the only screen with no backend calls — a product extension.)*

---

## 8. Data model (reference)

Main entities of the backend (Supabase / Postgres). Field names are reference suggestions, not mandatory character by character. **Where this table differs from the API contract (`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`), the contract prevails** (see section 6).

| Table | Main fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `users` | id, email, biometric_enabled, persona, created_at | RLS: a user accesses only their own row |
| `entries` | id, user_id, content, source (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), chat_message_id (nullable), embedding (vector, see 9), sync_status, created_at, updated_at | `embedding` generated in `POST /entries` via Voyage AI |
| `tags` | id, user_id, name | Extension — created manually by the user |
| `entry_tags` | entry_id, tag_id | N:N join table |
| `chat_sessions` | id, user_id, title, created_at | — |
| `chat_messages` | id, session_id, role (`user`/`assistant`), content, created_at | User messages show the RF10 button |
| `export_jobs` | id, user_id, status (`pending`/`processing`/`done`/`error`), period_start, period_end, file_url, created_at | Asynchronous — see 6.5 |

**RLS pattern (every table with `user_id`):** policy `auth.uid() = user_id`, no exceptions.

---

## 9. Technology stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Mobile app | Flutter, BLoC, Clean Architecture |
| Backend | Already built and frozen; consumed through its API |
| Infrastructure | Supabase (Postgres + pgvector + Storage + Auth + RLS) |
| Chat / vision / OCR / summary / insights / dashboard / PII | Claude Sonnet 5 (chat) + Claude Haiku 4.5 (the rest) — in the backend |
| Embeddings (RAG) | Voyage AI `voyage-4` — in the backend |
| Speech-to-text (audio transcription) | Whisper on-device (`whisper_ggml`); audio never reaches the backend |
| Error handling | `fpdart` (`Either<Failure, T>`) |
| Layer rule | RNF06 |
| Test coverage | RNF07 |

---

## 10. Configuration parameters

Fixed values — not to be reinterpreted.

| Parameter | Value | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Background session timeout | 5 min | RF03 |
| Search debounce | 300 ms | RF06 |
| Proactive insight trigger | 5 messages OR 2 min of inactivity | RF08 |
| Dashboard rendering scenarios | 0 / 1 / > 30 entries | RF09 |
| Minimum test coverage (domain) | ≥ 80% | RNF07 |
| Local UI latency | < 100 ms | RNF01 |
| Loading-indicator threshold | > 300 ms | RNF01 |
| Network-error scenarios tested | 5 endpoints × 3 failures = 15 | RNF09 |

---

## 11. Error codes (RNF09)

Every endpoint returns `{ code, message, retryable }`. Minimum codes the app handles:

| Code | Situation | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |

The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.

---

## 12. Delivery order

Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:

**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

---

## 13. Technical constraints

**Fixed:**
- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
- Folder convention:

```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```

**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.

1	# Implementation Plan: P-RF05 — Personal summary export
2	
3	**Branch**: `010-personal-summary-export` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's
4	extension hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)
5	
6	**Date**: 2026-10-24 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
7	
8	**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/010-personal-summary-export/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md`
9	§1 (RF05), §6.5 (`export-summary-create`/`export-status-get`/`export-download-get`), §8 (data model
10	reference), §9 (stack), §13; `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/export/*` schemas;
11	`docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`;
12	`docs/input/backend/README.md`'s function-name mapping; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §2.5; and
13	`.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on RF07 (`specs/005-multi-source-timeline/`), already implemented —
14	this is the unit that makes "Meus Registros"' currently-inert download icon
15	(`records_page.dart`'s `_Header`, comment "no export behavior in this unit") actually work.
16	
17	## Summary
18	
19	"Meus Registros"' download icon gains a bottom sheet (`ExportSheet`) that requests an async export job for
20	whatever period the screen's own active date filter represents (`POST /export/summary`), polls its status
21	(`GET /export/{jobId}/status`) every 2 seconds, and — once the job reaches a terminal state — offers a PDF
22	narrative download and/or a raw-data download (`GET /export/{jobId}/download`), each saved/shared via the OS
23	share sheet. A new feature folder, `lib/features/export/`, is added with its own three-layer structure:
24	`ExportJob`/`ExportFormat`/`ExportSheetState` (domain, plus a pure `sheetState` derivation of
25	`export-screen-states.md`'s table), `ExportRepository`/`ExportFileRepository` (domain interfaces),
26	`ExportRemoteDataSource`/`ExportRepositoryImpl`/`ExportFileRepositoryImpl` (data), and one bloc, `ExportBloc`
27	(one new instance per sheet open, research.md R6). `core/network/ApiClient` gains one new, export-agnostic
28	method, `downloadFile()` — a two-step fetch (our backend's 302, then a header-less GET of the signed Storage
29	URL) that never forwards this app's own credentials to the Storage host (research.md R1). A new dependency,
30	`share_plus`, provides the "save or share" affordance no existing package in this app covers. The spec's own
31	resolved Clarification — a sixth, generic failure state distinct from the prototype's one narrative-only
32	"Erro" — is implemented as a sixth `ExportSheetState`/`ExportState` value, `erroCompleto`/`ExportFailed`
33	(research.md R4). `records_page.dart`'s `_Header`/`_RecordsPageState` are extended in place to wire the icon
34	to the sheet, deriving the period from `RecordsBloc`'s existing `DateRangeOption` via RF06's own
35	`DateRangeBounds` extension (research.md R8) — no new `RecordsBloc` event/state, no new `go_router` route.
36	
37	## Technical Context
38	
39	**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
40	F000/RF01/RF03/RF06/RF07.
41	
42	**Primary Dependencies**: One addition — `share_plus: ^13.3.1` (research.md R2), the OS share sheet for the
43	two downloadable files this unit produces. Everything else reuses the full existing stack —
44	`flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`, `equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, extended with `downloadFile()`),
45	`path_provider` (already present for the audio pipeline, reused here for a temp file), `go_router` (no new
46	route); dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`.
47	
48	**Storage**: None new. `export_jobs`/their downloaded files are explicitly ephemeral (Key Entities: "never
49	shown anywhere outside the export sheet") — unlike `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`, this unit adds no
50	on-device persistence; a downloaded file lives only in the OS temp directory for the lifetime of the share
51	sheet.
52	
53	**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via `fvm flutter test
54	--coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now additionally exercising `export_job.dart`'s pure
55	`sheetState` mapping (R4), `ExportRepositoryImpl`'s silent-refresh-and-retry branches (reused verbatim from
56	`EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s shape), and `ApiClient.downloadFile()`'s two-leg redirect/fetch logic (a `core/`
57	addition — `test/core/network/`, mirroring where `sse_frame`/`error_mapper` tests already live).
58	
59	**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. No native project file touched beyond whatever
60	`share_plus`'s own iOS integration requires at the `Info.plist`/Podfile level (its own install instructions;
61	no custom native code written by this unit).
62	
63	**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app. One new feature folder, `lib/features/export/`
64	(domain/data/presentation, Principle V), one cross-cutting `core/network/` addition
65	(`ApiClient.downloadFile()`), and in-place extensions to `lib/features/records/presentation/pages/
66	records_page.dart` (`_Header`/`_RecordsPageState`, research.md R8) and `lib/core/di/service_locator.dart`. No
67	backend/server code, no change to `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`.
68	
69	**Performance Goals**: RNF01 unchanged. The sheet's "Pendente" state appears synchronously the instant the
70	download icon is tapped (before the `POST` even resolves), satisfying "a local action is reflected in the UI
71	in under 100 ms"; the `POST`/polling/download calls themselves are each already covered by the loading-
72	indicator convention their own sheet states already are (spinner/progress bar), satisfying "any network call
73	taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a loading indicator" by construction — there is no network call in this
74	unit's flow that is ever silent.
75	
76	**Constraints**:
77	- No manual-tag/category filtering or any other extension feature (FR-013) — the export sheet has no period
78	  picker, no persona/categorization control of its own.
79	- No functionality belonging to a unit later than RF05 in the build order (FR-013) — RF09's dashboard
80	  narrative (`GET /dashboard/narrative`) is a distinct endpoint, never touched here.
81	- No backend/contract/config change (FR-013) — `downloadFile()`'s two-leg shape and every parsed field name
82	  (research.md R1/contracts/export-repository.md) are this app's own typed wrapper around what
83	  `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` already describes.
84	- Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature (Principle V) — `export/domain/` imports only
85	  `equatable`/`fpdart`; no `package:flutter`, no `export/data/` class. `ExportBloc` depends only on
86	  `ExportRepository`/`ExportFileRepository` — never `SessionRepository` directly (research.md R7), never
87	  `RecordsBloc` (no cross-bloc import).
88	- FR-011's concurrency guard is satisfied by construction, not by a shared/persisted job id: a sheet-scoped,
89	  `registerFactory`-registered `ExportBloc` (research.md R6) plus a simple tap-guard in
90	  `_RecordsPageState` (research.md R8/contracts/records-header-export-extension.md) — no second
91	  `POST /export/summary` can fire for the same tap, and no in-flight job is polled once its sheet is gone.
92	- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — every new widget
93	  reuses existing tokens only (data-model.md's widget list) — zero new color/spacing/radius tokens needed,
94	  since `colorAccent`/`colorSuccess`/`colorError` already exist from F000/RF06/RF07.
95	
96	**Scale/Scope**: 1 new feature folder (`export/`) with 1 domain entity + 1 pure derivation extension, 2
97	repository interfaces, 2 data classes + 2 repository impls, 1 bloc (+events/states), 7 new presentation
98	widgets; 1 extended `core/network/` method (`ApiClient.downloadFile()`); 1 existing `records/` file extended
99	in place (`records_page.dart`); 1 new dependency (`share_plus`); 5 new DI registrations.
100	
101	## Constitution Check
102	
103	*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-checked after Phase 1 design — see bottom of this section.*
104	
105	| Principle / Standard | Status | Notes |
106	|---|---|---|
107	| I. Product Source of Truth | PASS | `docs/input/` read-only. Every spot this plan resolves by reasonable technical judgment rather than reopening spec.md's own already-resolved Clarification (the FR-007 sixth state) — the download-transport mechanism (research.md R1), the file-save/share package (R2), the poll interval (R3), the sheet-state derivation and its sixth value (R4), routing non-empty-period `POST` failures to FR-007 (R5), the sheet-scoped-bloc concurrency shape (R6), the reauth wiring (R7), and period-bounds plumbing (R8) — is each built directly on spec.md's own FRs/Assumptions/Key Entities wording, never reopening the resolved Clarification. |
108	| II. Fixed Technology Stack | PASS | No change to `flutter_bloc`/`fpdart`/`get_it`/Clean Architecture.
