**Branch**: `010-personal-summary-export` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's
extension hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)

**Date**: 2026-10-24 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/010-personal-summary-export/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md`
§1 (RF05), §6.5 (`export-summary-create`/`export-status-get`/`export-download-get`), §8 (data model
reference), §9 (stack), §13; `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/export/*` schemas;
`docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`;
`docs/input/backend/README.md`'s function-name mapping; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §2.5; and
`.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on RF07 (`specs/005-multi-source-timeline/`), already implemented —
this is the unit that makes "Meus Registros"' currently-inert download icon
(`records_page.dart`'s `_Header`, comment "no export behavior in this unit") actually work.

## Summary

"Meus Registros"' download icon gains a bottom sheet (`ExportSheet`) that requests an async export job for
whatever period the screen's own active date filter represents (`POST /export/summary`), polls its status
(`GET /export/{jobId}/status`) every 2 seconds, and — once the job reaches a terminal state — offers a PDF
narrative download and/or a raw-data download (`GET /export/{jobId}/download`), each saved/shared via the OS
share sheet. A new feature folder, `lib/features/export/`, is added with its own three-layer structure:
`ExportJob`/`ExportFormat`/`ExportSheetState` (domain, plus a pure `sheetState` derivation of
`export-screen-states.md`'s table), `ExportRepository`/`ExportFileRepository` (domain interfaces),
`ExportRemoteDataSource`/`ExportRepositoryImpl`/`ExportFileRepositoryImpl` (data), and one bloc, `ExportBloc`
(one new instance per sheet open, research.md R6). `core/network/ApiClient` gains one new, export-agnostic
method, `downloadFile()` — a two-step fetch (our backend's 302, then a header-less GET of the signed Storage
URL) that never forwards this app's own credentials to the Storage host (research.md R1). A new dependency,
`share_plus`, provides the "save or share" affordance no existing package in this app covers. The spec's own
resolved Clarification — a sixth, generic failure state distinct from the prototype's one narrative-only
"Erro" — is implemented as a sixth `ExportSheetState`/`ExportState` value, `erroCompleto`/`ExportFailed`
(research.md R4). `records_page.dart`'s `_Header`/`_RecordsPageState` are extended in place to wire the icon
to the sheet, deriving the period from `RecordsBloc`'s existing `DateRangeOption` via RF06's own
`DateRangeBounds` extension (research.md R8) — no new `RecordsBloc` event/state, no new `go_router` route.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
F000/RF01/RF03/RF06/RF07.

**Primary Dependencies**: One addition — `share_plus: ^13.3.1` (research.md R2), the OS share sheet for the
two downloadable files this unit produces. Everything else reuses the full existing stack —
`flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`, `equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, extended with `downloadFile()`),
`path_provider` (already present for the audio pipeline, reused here for a temp file), `go_router` (no new
route); dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`.

**Storage**: None new. `export_jobs`/their downloaded files are explicitly ephemeral (Key Entities: "never
shown anywhere outside the export sheet") — unlike `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`, this unit adds no
on-device persistence; a downloaded file lives only in the OS temp directory for the lifetime of the share
sheet.

**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via `fvm flutter test
--coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now additionally exercising `export_job.dart`'s pure
`sheetState` mapping (R4), `ExportRepositoryImpl`'s silent-refresh-and-retry branches (reused verbatim from
`EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s shape), and `ApiClient.downloadFile()`'s two-leg redirect/fetch logic (a `core/`
addition — `test/core/network/`, mirroring where `sse_frame`/`error_mapper` tests already live).

**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. No native project file touched beyond whatever
`share_plus`'s own iOS integration requires at the `Info.plist`/Podfile level (its own install instructions;
no custom native code written by this unit).

**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app. One new feature folder, `lib/features/export/`
(domain/data/presentation, Principle V), one cross-cutting `core/network/` addition
(`ApiClient.downloadFile()`), and in-place extensions to `lib/features/records/presentation/pages/
records_page.dart` (`_Header`/`_RecordsPageState`, research.md R8) and `lib/core/di/service_locator.dart`. No
backend/server code, no change to `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`.

**Performance Goals**: RNF01 unchanged. The sheet's "Pendente" state appears synchronously the instant the
download icon is tapped (before the `POST` even resolves), satisfying "a local action is reflected in the UI
in under 100 ms"; the `POST`/polling/download calls themselves are each already covered by the loading-
indicator convention their own sheet states already are (spinner/progress bar), satisfying "any network call
taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a loading indicator" by construction — there is no network call in this
unit's flow that is ever silent.

**Constraints**:
- No manual-tag/category filtering or any other extension feature (FR-013) — the export sheet has no period
  picker, no persona/categorization control of its own.
- No functionality belonging to a unit later than RF05 in the build order (FR-013) — RF09's dashboard
  narrative (`GET /dashboard/narrative`) is a distinct endpoint, never touched here.

  since `colorAccent`/`colorSuccess`/`colorError` already exist from F000/RF06/RF07.

repository interfaces, 2 data classes + 2 repository impls, 1 bloc (+events/states), 7 new presentation
widgets; 1 extended `core/network/` method (`ApiClient.downloadFile()`); 1 existing `records/` file extended

        │           ├── export_concluded_view.dart          # NEW
        │           ├── export_narrative_failed_view.dart   # NEW
        │           ├── export_failed_view.dart              # NEW
        │           └── export_empty_period_view.dart        # NEW
        └── records/
            └── presentation/
                └── pages/
                    └── records_page.dart                   # extended — _Header/_RecordsPageState wiring
```

**Structure Decision**: One new feature folder, `export/`, following the exact three-layer convention every
prior unit already established — no deviation. The one `core/network/` addition (`ApiClient.downloadFile()`)
lives there rather than inside `export/` because it is not export-specific in shape (any future signed-URL-
download unit reuses it as-is, same reasoning RF04's `sseStream()` was placed in `core/network/` rather than
inside `chat/`). `records/` is extended rather than having the export sheet folded into it because the sheet
is its own independently-testable concern (its own bloc, its own repository boundary) that only happens to be
*opened from* "Meus Registros" — exactly the same "extend the opening screen in place, give the new concern
its own feature folder" shape RF06's `FilterSheet` already established within `records/` itself (the one
difference being `FilterSheet` has no bloc of its own, needing no separate feature folder, while the export
sheet's async job/polling/download concern is large enough to warrant one, mirroring `chat/`'s own
`AppDrawer`-extension-plus-new-feature-folder precedent).

## Complexity Tracking

| Addition | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
|---|---|---|
| A second `ApiClient` transport primitive, `downloadFile()` (research.md R1) | `export-download-get` is this app's first endpoint whose success response is a 302-to-a-signed-URL, not JSON — `call()`'s existing `Dio.request<Map<String, dynamic>>()` cannot parse a redirect target's binary bytes, and naively letting `dio` auto-follow the redirect would forward this app's own auth headers to a third-party Storage host | Letting `dio` auto-follow redirects and reusing `call()` as-is — rejected: leaks `apikey`/bearer-token headers to a host they were never scoped for (research.md R1) |
| A new dependency, `share_plus` | This app has no existing mechanism for "hand the user a file to save or share" — `path_provider` alone only produces a path, never a UI affordance to do anything with it | Writing to a permanent path with no share prompt — rejected, a dead end with no in-app file viewer in scope (research.md R2) |
| A sixth `ExportSheetState`/`ExportState` value (`erroCompleto`/`ExportFailed`), beyond the prototype's five named states | The resolved Clarification explicitly requires a failure state "visually and functionally distinct" from the prototype's one narrative-only "Erro" — collapsing both into one state with a flag would directly contradict that resolution | One shared `erro` state with a boolean "is this the narrative-only case" flag — rejected per the Clarification's own explicit wording (research.md R4) |

*No entry needed beyond these three — each is either this unit's first genuinely new mechanism (the
redirect-download transport, the file-share dependency) or a direct, required encoding of spec.md's own
already-resolved Clarification (the sixth state).*

## Post-Design Constitution Check

Re-evaluated after Phase 1 (data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md):

- `export/domain/entities/export_job.dart` and both `export/domain/repositories/*.dart` were re-checked
  against their actual planned imports: `equatable`, `fpdart` (for `Either`/`Unit` signatures), and
  `core/network/failure.dart` only. No `package:flutter`, no `export/data/` class — RNF06/Principle V
  confirmed before any code exists.
- `ExportBloc`'s dependency surface was re-checked: exactly `ExportRepository` + `ExportFileRepository` — no
  `SessionRepository`, no `RecordsBloc` import. Neither `ExportBloc` nor `RecordsBloc` appears in the other's
  planned import list (`no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart` covers this mechanically across `features/` folders).
- Re-checked `ApiClient.downloadFile()`'s exception handling against `call()`'s existing `_mapException` —
  reused verbatim for leg 1; leg 2's storage-host failures fall through the same function's existing no-JSON-
  body branch, so no second, divergent failure-mapping implementation was introduced.
- Re-checked that the second `_dio.request` in `downloadFile()` (the storage leg) sends no
  `apikey`/`Authorization` header at all — confirmed in `contracts/http-client-download-extension.md`'s own
  code listing (Principle III's credential-exposure concern, research.md R1).
- Re-checked that `ExportJob.sheetState`, the one domain helper RNF07 specifically needs to be independently
  testable, has zero constructor dependencies and zero I/O — confirmed pure in data-model.md's own listing.
- Re-checked the `records_page.dart` extension (research.md R8) against Principle V: no new `RecordsEvent`/
  `RecordsState`, no new `go_router` route — `AppRoutes.records` itself is unchanged, and `_Header`'s only
  new dependency is a `VoidCallback` its own parent already owns.
- No change surfaces that touches `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, `.env`, any native iOS project file
  beyond `share_plus`'s own documented install step, or calls an AI provider directly — Principle III remains
  intact. No export code path reaches a manual-tag/category filter or any RF09-owned endpoint — FR-013 holds
  by construction (confirmed by `export/`'s own planned import list containing nothing from
  `features/entries/` tag handling or `dashboard`-shaped calls).

No new violations. Gate remains PASS.

specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:15:- Q: During first-time PIN setup, if the user opts into Face ID/Touch ID and the `PATCH /account/settings` call to save `biometricEnabled` fails (timeout, no connection, etc.), should that block the user from reaching Home/Chat, or should the app proceed locally and let the write resolve/retry in the background? → A: Proceed locally and retry in the background — the local PIN and the on-device biometric toggle already work regardless of backend reachability; first-time setup does not block on this write succeeding, consistent with the local-first philosophy of FR-002 and FR-015 (resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I).
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:25:**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by launching the app on a device with biometrics enrolled and the vault already configured, confirming the biometric prompt appears before any data is visible, and confirming a successful scan proceeds into the app's normal session routing.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:29:1. **Given** a device with a PIN already configured and Face ID/Touch ID enabled, **When** the app is cold-launched, **Then** the biometric prompt appears before any journal or chat content is shown, and a successful scan proceeds to the app's existing session routing (Home/Chat or login, depending on session validity).
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:30:2. **Given** the app was sent to the background and brought back after 5 minutes or more, **When** it resumes, **Then** the biometric prompt appears again before the previous screen becomes visible or interactive.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:39:**Why this priority**: Explicit acceptance criterion in the requirement — a failed biometric read must never lock the user out, since biometric sensors fail routinely under normal conditions.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:41:**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a biometric failure (denied, cancelled, or not recognized) and confirming the PIN screen appears with an error message, then confirming a correct PIN still unlocks the app.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:45:1. **Given** the biometric prompt is shown, **When** the scan fails or is not recognized, **Then** the PIN entry screen appears showing the error message "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN", without any other interruption.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:46:2. **Given** the PIN screen shown after a biometric failure, **When** the user enters the correct 4-digit PIN, **Then** the app unlocks and proceeds normally.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:47:3. **Given** the PIN screen shown after a biometric failure, **When** the user enters an incorrect PIN, **Then** the error state remains, the entered digits are cleared, and the user can try again with no limit that locks them out of the app entirely.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:53:Right after a user's very first successful login or sign-up on a device, before they can use the app, they are asked to choose a 4-digit PIN and confirm it. This PIN becomes the fallback that always works, whether or not biometrics are set up.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:64:4. **Given** the device supports Face ID or Touch ID, **When** PIN setup completes, **Then** the user is offered the option to also enable biometric unlock, and their choice is saved as their biometrics preference.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:70:A user who cannot pass biometrics or does not remember their PIN taps a visible link on the vault screen and is taken to the regular email/password login, regaining access that way instead of being stuck.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:78:1. **Given** the vault screen (biometric or PIN) is shown, **When** the user taps "usar e-mail e senha", **Then** they are taken to the existing login screen.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:85:- A device has no biometric hardware, or no fingerprint/face enrolled at the OS level: the vault shows the PIN screen directly as the only method, without attempting or showing a fingerprint prompt first.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:87:- A user disables biometrics at the OS level (outside the app) between sessions: the next vault appearance falls back to PIN entry directly, with no error shown for the missing biometric capability.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:91:- The `PATCH /account/settings` call that saves the biometrics preference during first-time setup fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response): PIN setup still completes and the user still reaches Home/Chat; the write is not retried synchronously as part of the setup flow.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:98:- **FR-002**: The system MUST perform this authentication entirely on-device; no biometric data and no PIN value may be sent to, or validated by, the backend.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:99:- **FR-003**: When biometrics are enabled and available on the device, the system MUST attempt Face ID/Touch ID first; when biometrics are unavailable (no hardware, nothing enrolled, or disabled), the system MUST present PIN entry as the method shown, without attempting a biometric prompt.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:100:- **FR-004**: When a biometric attempt fails or is not recognized, the system MUST immediately offer PIN entry as an alternative, together with the error message "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN", and MUST NOT lock the user out of attempting authentication again.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:102:- **FR-006**: The vault screen MUST offer a visible link ("usar e-mail e senha") that leads to the existing email/password login screen, for cases where neither biometrics nor the PIN can be used.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:109:- **FR-013**: On a device where biometrics are available, the system MUST let the user optionally enable Face ID/Touch ID unlock as part of first-time PIN setup, and MUST persist that choice as the account's biometrics preference through the backend.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:110:- **FR-014**: Persisting the biometrics preference MUST reuse the single typed-failure network call path already established by the foundation unit, not a separate or ad hoc HTTP call. If that call fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the failure MUST NOT block PIN setup from completing or the user from reaching Home/Chat — the local PIN and the on-device biometric toggle already govern unlocking regardless of backend reachability, and the preference write is left to resolve or retry through the existing failure-handling path.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:112:- **FR-016**: This unit MUST NOT implement the functional behavior of any later-delivered requirement (RF01, RF02, RF04 through RF10), including building the Settings screen; any biometrics control beyond first-time setup is out of scope.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:113:- **FR-017**: This unit MUST NOT implement any extension feature (manual tags, action plans, persona selection).
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:120:- **Biometrics Preference**: An account-level flag (`biometricEnabled`) indicating whether Face ID/Touch ID is the user's enrolled unlock method; read and written through the backend's account-settings endpoint, but never the thing that performs the actual biometric check.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:128:- **SC-003**: A user whose biometric attempt fails can always reach their data via PIN in the same session — 0 cases where a biometric failure alone ends in the user being unable to proceed.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:135:- A dedicated toggle to change the biometrics preference later (outside of first-time setup) belongs to the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit; this unit implements the account-settings read/write path for `biometricEnabled` but not that screen's UI.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:140:- Device biometric availability (hardware present, something enrolled, not disabled) is read from the platform's own biometrics API; this unit does not reimplement that detection.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:141:- The Face ID/Touch ID prompt is triggered automatically as soon as the vault screen with biometrics enabled appears (standard platform behavior), not only after a tap; the fingerprint circle and "Toque para desbloquear" act as a manual retry affordance for when the OS prompt was dismissed or cancelled, consistent with User Story 1's requirement that the prompt appear before any data is shown on cold launch.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:142:- When a user disables biometrics at the OS level between sessions (see Edge Cases), this unit does not call the backend to flip `biometricEnabled` to false; the account-level preference is only ever written during first-time setup (FR-013) in this unit, and keeping it in sync with later out-of-band OS changes is left to the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit, consistent with the existing assumption that a dedicated toggle belongs there.

specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:46:2. **Given** the PIN screen shown after a biometric failure, **When** the user enters the correct 4-digit PIN, **Then** the app unlocks and proceeds normally.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:47:3. **Given** the PIN screen shown after a biometric failure, **When** the user enters an incorrect PIN, **Then** the error state remains, the entered digits are cleared, and the user can try again with no limit that locks them out of the app entirely.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:53:Right after a user's very first successful login or sign-up on a device, before they can use the app, they are asked to choose a 4-digit PIN and confirm it. This PIN becomes the fallback that always works, whether or not biometrics are set up.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:64:4. **Given** the device supports Face ID or Touch ID, **When** PIN setup completes, **Then** the user is offered the option to also enable biometric unlock, and their choice is saved as their biometrics preference.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:70:A user who cannot pass biometrics or does not remember their PIN taps a visible link on the vault screen and is taken to the regular email/password login, regaining access that way instead of being stuck.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:78:1. **Given** the vault screen (biometric or PIN) is shown, **When** the user taps "usar e-mail e senha", **Then** they are taken to the existing login screen.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:85:- A device has no biometric hardware, or no fingerprint/face enrolled at the OS level: the vault shows the PIN screen directly as the only method, without attempting or showing a fingerprint prompt first.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:87:- A user disables biometrics at the OS level (outside the app) between sessions: the next vault appearance falls back to PIN entry directly, with no error shown for the missing biometric capability.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:91:- The `PATCH /account/settings` call that saves the biometrics preference during first-time setup fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response): PIN setup still completes and the user still reaches Home/Chat; the write is not retried synchronously as part of the setup flow.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:98:- **FR-002**: The system MUST perform this authentication entirely on-device; no biometric data and no PIN value may be sent to, or validated by, the backend.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:99:- **FR-003**: When biometrics are enabled and available on the device, the system MUST attempt Face ID/Touch ID first; when biometrics are unavailable (no hardware, nothing enrolled, or disabled), the system MUST present PIN entry as the method shown, without attempting a biometric prompt.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:100:- **FR-004**: When a biometric attempt fails or is not recognized, the system MUST immediately offer PIN entry as an alternative, together with the error message "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN", and MUST NOT lock the user out of attempting authentication again.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:102:- **FR-006**: The vault screen MUST offer a visible link ("usar e-mail e senha") that leads to the existing email/password login screen, for cases where neither biometrics nor the PIN can be used.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:109:- **FR-013**: On a device where biometrics are available, the system MUST let the user optionally enable Face ID/Touch ID unlock as part of first-time PIN setup, and MUST persist that choice as the account's biometrics preference through the backend.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:110:- **FR-014**: Persisting the biometrics preference MUST reuse the single typed-failure network call path already established by the foundation unit, not a separate or ad hoc HTTP call. If that call fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the failure MUST NOT block PIN setup from completing or the user from reaching Home/Chat — the local PIN and the on-device biometric toggle already govern unlocking regardless of backend reachability, and the preference write is left to resolve or retry through the existing failure-handling path.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:112:- **FR-016**: This unit MUST NOT implement the functional behavior of any later-delivered requirement (RF01, RF02, RF04 through RF10), including building the Settings screen; any biometrics control beyond first-time setup is out of scope.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:113:- **FR-017**: This unit MUST NOT implement any extension feature (manual tags, action plans, persona selection).
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:120:- **Biometrics Preference**: An account-level flag (`biometricEnabled`) indicating whether Face ID/Touch ID is the user's enrolled unlock method; read and written through the backend's account-settings endpoint, but never the thing that performs the actual biometric check.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:128:- **SC-003**: A user whose biometric attempt fails can always reach their data via PIN in the same session — 0 cases where a biometric failure alone ends in the user being unable to proceed.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:135:- A dedicated toggle to change the biometrics preference later (outside of first-time setup) belongs to the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit; this unit implements the account-settings read/write path for `biometricEnabled` but not that screen's UI.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:140:- Device biometric availability (hardware present, something enrolled, not disabled) is read from the platform's own biometrics API; this unit does not reimplement that detection.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:141:- The Face ID/Touch ID prompt is triggered automatically as soon as the vault screen with biometrics enabled appears (standard platform behavior), not only after a tap; the fingerprint circle and "Toque para desbloquear" act as a manual retry affordance for when the OS prompt was dismissed or cancelled, consistent with User Story 1's requirement that the prompt appear before any data is shown on cold launch.
specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md:142:- When a user disables biometrics at the OS level between sessions (see Edge Cases), this unit does not call the backend to flip `biometricEnabled` to false; the account-level preference is only ever written during first-time setup (FR-013) in this unit, and keeping it in sync with later out-of-band OS changes is left to the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit, consistent with the existing assumption that a dedicated toggle belongs there.

1	import 'dart:convert';
2	
3	import 'package:cerne/features/entries/domain/entities/entry.dart';
4	import 'package:flutter_secure_storage/flutter_secure_storage.dart';
5	
6	/// On-device, cross-restart persistence for the entries the user has
7	/// already seen (the PRD's "local read cache" — requirements.md line 50/125:
8	/// results from it stay visible offline and reconcile with the server on
9	/// reconnect, with no duplicates). Keychain-backed, same pattern as
10	/// `VaultSecureStorage` — journal content is personal data, so it stays
11	/// encrypted at rest like the PIN it already sits behind.
12	///
13	/// Distinct from `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s in-memory `cachedEntries`: that
14	/// field only ever held optimistic just-created entries for this process's
15	/// lifetime (research.md R8, 003-multimodal-capture). This class is what
16	/// makes that same list survive an app restart, which is what a cold open
17	/// on an already-offline device needs (closing snapshot at unit completion
18	/// did not cover this path — see Meus Registros intervention report).
19	class EntriesLocalCache {
20	  EntriesLocalCache({FlutterSecureStorage? storage})
21	    : _storage = storage ?? const FlutterSecureStorage();
22	
23	  final FlutterSecureStorage _storage;
24	
25	  static const _key = 'entriesLocalCache';
26	
27	  Future<List<Entry>> readAll() async {
28	    final raw = await _storage.read(key: _key);
29	    if (raw == null) return const [];
30	    try {
31	      final decoded = jsonDecode(raw) as List<dynamic>;
32	      return decoded.map((e) => _fromJson(e as Map<String, dynamic>)).toList();
33	    } on FormatException {
34	      return const [];
35	    } on TypeError {
36	      return const [];
37	    }
38	  }
39	
40	  Future<void> writeAll(List<Entry> entries) {
41	    final encoded = jsonEncode(entries.map(_toJson).toList());
42	    return _storage.write(key: _key, value: encoded);
43	  }
44	
45	  Map<String, dynamic> _toJson(Entry e) => {
46	    'id': e.id,
47	    'content': e.content,
48	    'source': e.source.name,
49	    'chatMessageId': e.chatMessageId,
50	    'occurredAt': e.occurredAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
51	    'tags': [
52	      for (final tag in e.tags) {'id': tag.id, 'name': tag.name},
53	    ],
54	    'piiStatus': e.piiStatus.name,
55	    'piiSpans': [
56	      for (final span in e.piiSpans)
57	        {'start': span.start, 'end': span.end, 'type': span.type},
58	    ],
59	    'embeddingStatus': e.embeddingStatus.name,
60	    'mediaDurationSeconds': e.mediaDurationSeconds,
61	    'serverRevision': e.serverRevision,
62	    'createdAt': e.createdAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
63	    'updatedAt': e.updatedAt.toUtc().toIso8601String(),
64	    'similarity': e.similarity,
65	  };
66	
67	  Entry _fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> data) => Entry(
68	    id: data['id'] as String,
69	    content: data['content'] as String,
70	    source: EntrySource.values.byName(data['source'] as String),
71	    chatMessageId: data['chatMessageId'] as String?,
72	    occurredAt: DateTime.parse(data['occurredAt'] as String),
73	    tags: (data['tags'] as List<dynamic>)
74	        .map(
75	          (t) => EntryTag(
76	            id: (t as Map<String, dynamic>)['id'] as String,
77	            name: t['name'] as String,
78	          ),
79	        )
80	        .toList(),
81	    piiStatus: PiiStatus.values.byName(data['piiStatus'] as String),
82	    piiSpans: (data['piiSpans'] as List<dynamic>)
83	        .map(
84	          (s) => PiiSpan(
85	            start: (s as Map<String, dynamic>)['start'] as int,
86	            end: s['end'] as int,
87	            type: s['type'] as String,
88	          ),
89	        )
90	        .toList(),
91	    embeddingStatus: EmbeddingStatus.values.byName(
92	      data['embeddingStatus'] as String,
93	    ),
94	    mediaDurationSeconds: data['mediaDurationSeconds'] as int?,
95	    serverRevision: data['serverRevision'] as int,
96	    createdAt: DateTime.parse(data['createdAt'] as String),
97	    updatedAt: DateTime.parse(data['updatedAt'] as String),
98	    similarity: (data['similarity'] as num?)?.toDouble(),
99	  );
100	}

95	### 2.5 Export (bottom sheet over Tela 4; 5 states)
96	| State | What it shows |
97	|---|---|
98	| Pendente | Spinner, "Preparando exportação...". |
99	| Processando | "Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar. |
100	| Concluído | Green check, "Resumo pronto", buttons "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline). |
101	| Erro | Red warning; text explaining that the AI narrative failed but the data remains available; only the button "Baixar dados brutos". |
102	| Período vazio | "Nenhum registro nesse período." and a suggestion to adjust the filter; no download button. |
103	
104	All five have the link "Fechar" at the bottom. The mapping between these states and the backend job statuses is in `docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`.
105	
106	### 2.6 Plans and settings
107	| State | What it shows |
108	|---|---|
109	| Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]** | Three horizontally scrolling columns — "A Fazer", "Em Andamento", "Concluído" — with counts and cards. |
110	| Tela 6 — Configurações — mais de 30 registros | "Sua evolução": 10-bar ochre chart + summary paragraph. |
111	| Tela 6 — Configurações — uma entrada | A single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias." |
112	| Tela 6 — Configurações — zero entradas | Light-gray chart icon in place of the chart and "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui"; no summary paragraph. |
113	| Tela 6 — Configurações — narrativa indisponível | Chart with data, but the AI summary paragraph failed — needs its own error message, not just missing text. |
114	| Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta | Centered dialog, red title "Apagar sua conta?", text on permanent, irreversible deletion; red button "Apagar tudo"; outline "Cancelar". |
115	
116	Other elements of Configurações: avatar with editable name/e-mail (pencil becomes a check in edit mode — inline editing); persona cards "Como a IA responde" (Analítico, Empático, Socrático) **[ext]**; actions "Sair" and "Apagar conta" (red).
117	
118	---
119	
120	## 3. Visual system (tokens for `design_tokens.dart`)
121	
122	The prototype has a **Design Tokens** panel, marked as the ground truth for `design_tokens.dart`. Its names and values are below.
123	
124	### Colors
125	| Token | Hex | Use (as stated in the panel) |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| `colorPrimary` | `#1F3D34` | Buttons, app bar, wordmark |
128	| `colorPrimaryPressed` | `#16281F` | Pressed state |
129	| `colorOnPrimary` | `#F5F1E8` | Text on primary |
130	| `colorAccent` | `#C98A3E` | CTA, insight, saved bookmark |
131	| `colorOnAccent` | `#241C0D` | Text on accent |
132	| `colorSecondary` | `#7C8B6F` | Tags, chips, synchronizing |
133	| `colorSurfaceBg` | `#F2EFE7` | General background ("paper") |
134	| `colorSurfaceElevated` | `#FBF9F4` | Cards, bubbles, sheets |
135	| `colorBorder` | `#E1DACB` | Dividers, borders |
136	| `colorTextPrimary` | `#241F19` | Main text |
137	| `colorTextSecondary` | `#6B6255` | Secondary text |
138	| `colorError` | `#B3402A` | Errors, destructive action |
139	| `colorSuccess` | `#4C6B4F` | Synchronized, confirmations |
140	| `colorWarningSync` | `#C98A3E` | "Synchronizing" badge |
141	| `colorInfoOffline` | `#5C7A93` | Offline banner — single use |
142	
143	Other colors that appear on specific screens but not in the panel: user chat bubble `#D9DFD3`; text on category chips `#3F4A38`.
144	
145	### Typography
146	| Token | Font · weight · size/line-height | Use |
147	|---|---|---|
148	| `textDisplayLg` | Fraunces 600 · 32/38 | Splash wordmark |
149	| `textHeadlineMd` | Fraunces 600 · 24/30 | Section titles |
150	| `textTitleLg` | Karla 700 · 20/26 | App bar title |
151	| `textTitleSm` | Karla 700 · 16/22 | Subtitles |
152	| `textBodyLg` | Karla 400 · 16/24 | Bubbles, entries |
153	| `textBodyMd` | Karla 400 · 14/20 | Secondary text and descriptions |
154	| `textLabelMd` | Karla 500 · 13/18 | Button text, chips |
155	| `textMonoCaption` | IBM Plex Mono 500 · 12/16 · letter-spacing .2 | Technical metadata (timestamps, counters, status labels) |
156	
157	### Spacing (4 dp grid)
158	`spacingXs` 4 · `spacingSm` 8 · `spacingMd` 16 · `spacingLg` 24 · `spacingXl` 32 · `spacing2xl` 48 (dp).
159	
160	### Radii
161	`radiusSm` 8 dp (inputs, chips) · `radiusMd` 16 dp (cards, bubbles) · `radiusLg` 24 dp (sheets, modals) · `radiusFull` 999 dp (avatars, pills).
162	
163	### Elevation
164	`elevation1` — `0 1px 3px rgba(36,31,25,.08)` (cards at rest) · `elevation2` — `0 4px 16px rgba(36,31,25,.14)` (sheets, modals).
165	
166	### Icons
167	Phosphor library, Regular style, 24 dp: `list`, `plus`, `magnifying-glass`, `funnel`, `bookmark-simple`, `microphone`, `camera`, `gear`, `kanban`, `notebook`, `fingerprint`, `lightbulb` (and others used on specific screens: `check`, `warning-circle`, `wifi-slash`, `circle-notch`, `caret-left`, `download-simple`, `pencil-simple`, `x`, `stop`, `image`, `check-circle`, `chart-line-up`, `backspace`, `lock-key`, `paper-plane-tilt`, `chat-circle-text`).
168	
169	### Spine (colored bar on the left of a card) — 3 contexts
170	1. Proactive insight in the chat — ochre.
171	2. Entry origin in "Meus Registros" — color by type: manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre.
172	3. Kanban column in "Planos de Ação" — color by column **[ext]**.
173	
174	### Micro-animations and transitions
175	- `scrimIn` (0.18 s ease-out): fade of the darkened background when any overlay opens.
176	- `sheetUp` (0.2 s ease-out): bottom sheets (insertion modal, filter, export) rise from the bottom of the screen.
177	- Continuous spinner (`spin`, 1 s linear infinite) in every loading state.
178	- Text streaming: the AI response is revealed progressively, with a blinking cursor at the end while it is "typing".
179	- PIN: after the 4th digit, a 350 ms pause before navigating.
180	
181	---
182	
183	## 4. Special states that need extra care
184	
185	- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
186	- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
187	- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
188	- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
189	- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
190	- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.
191	
192	---
193	
194	## 5. Implementation notes
195	
196	1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
197	2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
198	3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
199	4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
200	5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
201	6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
202	7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.
203	
204	---
205	
206	## 6. Component library
207	
208	| Component | Where it appears | Variations |
209	|---|---|---|
210	| Primary button | Auth, modals, sheets, confirmations | normal (`#1F3D34`) · pressed (`#16281F`, darker) · disabled (`#E1DACB` background, `#6B6255` text) |
211	| Secondary button (outline) | "Tentar novamente", "Cancelar", "Baixar dados brutos" | `#1F3D34` outline, no fill |
212	| Text button (ghost) | Mode-toggle links, "Fechar", "Limpar" | no background, `#1F3D34` or `#6B6255` depending on context |
213	| Text field | Login, Texto tab, name editing | empty · focused (1.5px `#1F3D34` border) · error (`#B3402A` border) |
214	| Chat bubble | Home/Chat | user (light green, straight bottom-right corner) · AI (ivory with shadow, straight bottom-left corner) · streaming (pulsing cursor at the end of the text) |

### 2.5 Export (bottom sheet over Tela 4; 5 states)
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Pendente | Spinner, "Preparando exportação...". |
| Processando | "Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar. |
| Concluído | Green check, "Resumo pronto", buttons "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline). |
| Erro | Red warning; text explaining that the AI narrative failed but the data remains available; only the button "Baixar dados brutos". |
| Período vazio | "Nenhum registro nesse período." and a suggestion to adjust the filter; no download button. |

All five have the link "Fechar" at the bottom. The mapping between these states and the backend job statuses is in `docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`.

### 2.6 Plans and settings
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]** | Three horizontally scrolling columns — "A Fazer", "Em Andamento", "Concluído" — with counts and cards. |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — mais de 30 registros | "Sua evolução": 10-bar ochre chart + summary paragraph. |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — uma entrada | A single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias." |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — zero entradas | Light-gray chart icon in place of the chart and "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui"; no summary paragraph. |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — narrativa indisponível | Chart with data, but the AI summary paragraph failed — needs its own error message, not just missing text. |
| Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta | Centered dialog, red title "Apagar sua conta?", text on permanent, irreversible deletion; red button "Apagar tudo"; outline "Cancelar". |

Other elements of Configurações: avatar with editable name/e-mail (pencil becomes a check in edit mode — inline editing); persona cards "Como a IA responde" (Analítico, Empático, Socrático) **[ext]**; actions "Sair" and "Apagar conta" (red).

---

## 3. Visual system (tokens for `design_tokens.dart`)

The prototype has a **Design Tokens** panel, marked as the ground truth for `design_tokens.dart`. Its names and values are below.

### Colors
| Token | Hex | Use (as stated in the panel) |
|---|---|---|
| `colorPrimary` | `#1F3D34` | Buttons, app bar, wordmark |
| `colorPrimaryPressed` | `#16281F` | Pressed state |
| `colorOnPrimary` | `#F5F1E8` | Text on primary |
| `colorAccent` | `#C98A3E` | CTA, insight, saved bookmark |
| `colorOnAccent` | `#241C0D` | Text on accent |
| `colorSecondary` | `#7C8B6F` | Tags, chips, synchronizing |
| `colorSurfaceBg` | `#F2EFE7` | General background ("paper") |
| `colorSurfaceElevated` | `#FBF9F4` | Cards, bubbles, sheets |
| `colorBorder` | `#E1DACB` | Dividers, borders |
| `colorTextPrimary` | `#241F19` | Main text |
| `colorTextSecondary` | `#6B6255` | Secondary text |
| `colorError` | `#B3402A` | Errors, destructive action |
| `colorSuccess` | `#4C6B4F` | Synchronized, confirmations |
| `colorWarningSync` | `#C98A3E` | "Synchronizing" badge |
| `colorInfoOffline` | `#5C7A93` | Offline banner — single use |

Other colors that appear on specific screens but not in the panel: user chat bubble `#D9DFD3`; text on category chips `#3F4A38`.

### Typography
| Token | Font · weight · size/line-height | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `textDisplayLg` | Fraunces 600 · 32/38 | Splash wordmark |
| `textHeadlineMd` | Fraunces 600 · 24/30 | Section titles |
| `textTitleLg` | Karla 700 · 20/26 | App bar title |
| `textTitleSm` | Karla 700 · 16/22 | Subtitles |
| `textBodyLg` | Karla 400 · 16/24 | Bubbles, entries |
| `textBodyMd` | Karla 400 · 14/20 | Secondary text and descriptions |
| `textLabelMd` | Karla 500 · 13/18 | Button text, chips |
| `textMonoCaption` | IBM Plex Mono 500 · 12/16 · letter-spacing .2 | Technical metadata (timestamps, counters, status labels) |

### Spacing (4 dp grid)
`spacingXs` 4 · `spacingSm` 8 · `spacingMd` 16 · `spacingLg` 24 · `spacingXl` 32 · `spacing2xl` 48 (dp).

### Radii
`radiusSm` 8 dp (inputs, chips) · `radiusMd` 16 dp (cards, bubbles) · `radiusLg` 24 dp (sheets, modals) · `radiusFull` 999 dp (avatars, pills).

### Elevation
`elevation1` — `0 1px 3px rgba(36,31,25,.08)` (cards at rest) · `elevation2` — `0 4px 16px rgba(36,31,25,.14)` (sheets, modals).

### Icons
Phosphor library, Regular style, 24 dp: `list`, `plus`, `magnifying-glass`, `funnel`, `bookmark-simple`, `microphone`, `camera`, `gear`, `kanban`, `notebook`, `fingerprint`, `lightbulb` (and others used on specific screens: `check`, `warning-circle`, `wifi-slash`, `circle-notch`, `caret-left`, `download-simple`, `pencil-simple`, `x`, `stop`, `image`, `check-circle`, `chart-line-up`, `backspace`, `lock-key`, `paper-plane-tilt`, `chat-circle-text`).

### Spine (colored bar on the left of a card) — 3 contexts
1. Proactive insight in the chat — ochre.
2. Entry origin in "Meus Registros" — color by type: manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre.
3. Kanban column in "Planos de Ação" — color by column **[ext]**.

### Micro-animations and transitions
- `scrimIn` (0.18 s ease-out): fade of the darkened background when any overlay opens.
- `sheetUp` (0.2 s ease-out): bottom sheets (insertion modal, filter, export) rise from the bottom of the screen.
- Continuous spinner (`spin`, 1 s linear infinite) in every loading state.
- Text streaming: the AI response is revealed progressively, with a blinking cursor at the end while it is "typing".
- PIN: after the 4th digit, a 350 ms pause before navigating.

---

## 4. Special states that need extra care

- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.

---

## 5. Implementation notes

1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.

# Research: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard

Phase 0 output. Each item is a technical-judgment decision this plan must make beyond what spec.md's own FRs/
Clarifications/Assumptions already resolve (Constitution Principle I: "where these documents are silent,
implementers MUST make a reasonable technical decision rather than block on clarification"). None of these
reopen a resolved Clarification; each builds directly on spec.md's own wording.

## R1 — Dashboard data flow is two independent repository calls, gated by `totals.count`

`DashboardRepository.fetchAggregate()` and `fetchNarrative()` are two separate methods, called separately by
`SettingsBloc`, never composed into one. The aggregate call always fires on `SettingsOpened`/retry (FR-001,
FR-008). The narrative call fires only after the aggregate succeeds **and** `aggregate.totals.count >= 2`
(FR-003/FR-004/FR-005) — the bloc inspects the already-resolved aggregate's own total, never a second network
round-trip to "find out" the count. Both calls send the single fixed query parameter `period=all` (spec.md
Assumption "Dashboard period") — no period parameter is ever user-controlled in this unit.

## R2 — Ten-bar bucketing is a pure, total function over `(buckets, today)`

Spec.md's Clarification/Assumption fixes the algorithm in words ("divide the account's full date range — date
of the first entry through today — into ten roughly-equal time slices and sum the per-date counts falling
within each slice"); this unit only has to fix the exact integer arithmetic so the function is deterministic
and testable:

```
List<int> tenBars(List<AggregateBucket> buckets, DateTime today) {
  if (buckets.isEmpty) return List.filled(10, 0);
  final start = buckets.map((b) => b.date).reduce((a, b) => a.isBefore(b) ? a : b);
  final totalDaySpan = today.difference(start).inDays; // >= 0; both date-only (UTC midnight)
  final bars = List.filled(10, 0);
  if (totalDaySpan == 0) {
    // Every entry happened "today" relative to the account's own first entry
    // (e.g. 2 entries created minutes apart) — a single-day range cannot be
    // divided into 10 meaningful slices, so the whole total lands in the
    // last bar rather than every bar collapsing onto index 0.
    bars[9] = buckets.fold(0, (sum, b) => sum + b.count);
    return bars;
  }
  for (final bucket in buckets) {
    final daysSinceStart = bucket.date.difference(start).inDays;
    final index = (daysSinceStart * 10) ~/ (totalDaySpan + 1);
    bars[index.clamp(0, 9)] += bucket.count;
  }
  return bars;
}
```
`totalDaySpan + 1` (not `totalDaySpan`) is the slice divisor so the very last day (`daysSinceStart ==
totalDaySpan`) still lands inside bar index 9, not spilling past it. This function is pure (no `DateTime.now()`
inside it — the caller passes `today`), lives in `domain/`, and is the one piece of this unit's logic RNF07
most needs to hit ≥80% on, mirroring `DateRangeFilter`/`SyncBadgeState`'s existing pure-derivation shape.

## R3 — No new charting dependency

The chart is always exactly 10 bars with no interaction (no tooltip, no zoom, no legend) — a `Row` of 10
`Container`s whose heights are `count / maxBarCount * DesignTokens.sizeChartBarMaxHeight` (clamped to a
minimum visible sliver for a non-zero, sub-pixel bar) already renders this losslessly with widgets the app
already depends on. Adding `fl_chart`/`syncfusion_flutter_charts`/etc. for 10 static bars would be the first
charting dependency in the app for a shape plain `Flutter` already draws — rejected (Complexity Tracking).
Principle II's "chart package" being a free/open choice means "free to add one if needed," not "must add one."

## R4 — `SettingsState` is one flat composite state, not a sealed per-mode hierarchy

Unlike `VaultBloc` (a strictly sequential state machine — PIN setup, then biometric prompt, then unlock) or
`ExportBloc` (one sheet, one job, mutually exclusive terminal states), Settings' four concerns — dashboard,
narrative, profile/name-edit, biometric toggle, sign-out, account-deletion — load and update **independently**
of one another on the same screen at the same time (e.g. the name can be mid-edit while the dashboard is still
loading). `SettingsState` is therefore one `Equatable` class with a field per concern and a `copyWith` using
the same `_unset` sentinel pattern `RecordsLoaded` already establishes for nullable fields that must be
explicitly clearable — the same shape, scaled to more independent regions, not a new pattern.

## R5 — Display-name caching: new, settings-owned local cache; biometric state: no new cache at all

Spec.md's "Account Profile" Key Entity requires treating "the most recent successful write... as the locally
held source of truth," including biometricEnabled, "defaulting sensibly... for an account that has never had
a successful write." Splitting this per field is simpler and more correct than a single shared cache:

- **`displayName`** has no on-device mirror anywhere else in the app — RF03 never writes it. A new
  `AccountProfileLocalCache` (`features/settings/data/`, Keychain-backed via `flutter_secure_storage`, same
  pattern as `VaultSecureStorage`/`EntriesLocalCache`) persists only the name this unit's own successful
  `PATCH` last confirmed. `AccountProfile.defaultDisplayNameFromEmail(email)` (see R13) supplies the sensible
  default when the cache is empty.
- **`biometricEnabled`** already has an authoritative, always-correct on-device mirror:
  `VaultRepository.isBiometricPreferenceEnabled()` (`VaultSecureStorage`), written synchronously during RF03's
  first-time setup regardless of whether that setup's own backend write succeeded (RF03 FR-014, local-first).
  Reading the toggle's initial state from there is *more* correct than inventing a second, settings-owned
  cache that RF03's write path would have to be taught to also populate — it is already "the most recent
  successful write" in the sense that matters (what the device itself currently enforces). No vault file needs
  to change for this unit to read it.

## R6 — Settings' own biometric-toggle write path: await + revert, reusing RF03's repository as-is

FR-014 ("the toggle MUST revert... rather than appearing to succeed") is the opposite contract from RF03's
existing `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` (`vault/domain/usecases/`), which is deliberately fire-and-forget
("always completes regardless of outcome" — RF03 research.md R6, first-time setup must never block on the
network). Rather than changing that usecase's contract (and risking RF03's own already-shipped behavior), this
unit adds a new, settings-owned usecase, `SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`
(`features/settings/domain/usecases/`), that:
1. calls `BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save(enabled)` (vault's existing, single-field repository — reused
   verbatim, not re-implemented — "continuing the account-settings read/write path RF03 already established
   for this same flag," FR-013's own wording) and *awaits* the `Either`;
2. on `Right`: calls `VaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally(enabled)` so the device's own unlock gate
   and Settings' displayed value move together;
3. on `Left`: returns the failure untouched — the local mirror is never written, so a later app relock still
   gates on the last-confirmed value, and `SettingsBloc` reverts the toggle's optimistic UI flip.

`BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/`BiometricsPreferenceRemoteDataSource` (vault/) are unmodified; this is a new
caller, not a new implementation.

## R7 — Display-name write path: new, narrow `AccountProfileRepository`

Mirrors `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`'s own documented reasoning ("deliberately narrow... rather than a
general-purpose account-settings repository"). A new `AccountSettingsRemoteDataSource.updateDisplayName()`
(`features/settings/data/`) sends `PATCH account-settings-update` with `{"displayName": ...}` only (never
`persona`, FR-015). `AccountProfileRepositoryImpl.updateDisplayName()` persists the confirmed name into
`AccountProfileLocalCache` before returning `Right` (FR-010, SC-005), and never touches `biometricEnabled` or
`persona` — a client-side-only `AccountProfile` validation (1–80 chars, FR-011) runs in the bloc before any
repository call, so an invalid name never reaches the network.

## R8 — Logout extends the existing `auth/` feature; account deletion is new, inside `settings/`

`POST /auth/logout` (`auth-logout`) is an auth-domain concern indistinguishable in shape from
`auth-signup`/`auth-login`, already owned by `AuthRepository`/`AuthRemoteDataSource`/`AuthRepositoryImpl`
(`features/auth/`) — this unit adds one method, `logout()`, to all three, the same "extend an earlier unit's
file in place" precedent RF05 already set on `records_page.dart`. `DELETE /account` (`account-delete`) is new
and squarely RF09/RNF05-owned, so it gets its own repository inside `features/settings/`
(`AccountDeletionRepository`/`AccountDeletionRemoteDataSource`/`AccountDeletionRepositoryImpl`), sending the
backend-required `{"confirmation": "DELETE"}` body the user never types (FR-018).

## R9 — What gets cleared locally: logout is narrower than account deletion, by FR text

FR-016 (Sair): "clear the local session and any cached account/profile state." FR-019 (Apagar conta): "clear
all local session, cached account/profile, **and any other locally held user data**." The extra clause in
FR-019 is read literally as a scope difference, not a wording accident — deleting the account is the LGPD hard
-delete path and must leave nothing recoverable; logging out from an account that still exists has no such
requirement. Concretely:

- **Both** actions clear `SessionRepository` (`SecureTokenStorage`'s 4 keys) and `AccountProfileLocalCache`
  (the cached display name) — the two "session" and "cached account/profile" nouns FR-016 itself names.
- **Only account deletion** additionally clears `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache` (both extended in place
  with a new `clear()` method, R14) and their owning repositories' in-memory mirrors (`EntriesRepository`/
  `ChatRepository` gain a `clearLocalData()` method each) — "any other locally held user data," FR-019.
- **Neither** action touches `VaultSecureStorage` (the device PIN hash or the biometrics-preference mirror) —
  see R10, this is deliberate and matches the prototype's own simulated destination.

## R10 — Post-logout/deletion destination: computed from `hasPinConfigured()`, reusing existing routes only

The prototype extract states both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to "Tela 0.1 — Biometria" — the same
destination (`prototype-extract.md` §1, §4.2). Spec.md's own Assumption resolves "the app's authentication
entry point" as "whatever F000/RF03 already resolve that case to (the vault screen if a device-level
PIN/biometric flow applies with no session, falling through to login otherwise) rather than building a
separate destination." The literal, minimal reading of that: `SettingsBloc` checks
`VaultRepository.hasPinConfigured()` after the session/profile clear and resolves to `AppRoutes.vault` (if
true) or `AppRoutes.login` (if false) — the same two routes `SplashPage` already builds its own routing
decision from, never a new route or screen. `SettingsPage` performs `context.go()` (not `push`) on the
resulting terminal state, discarding the whole Home/Settings back-stack, so there is no way to navigate back
into a signed-out Settings screen. Whatever happens *after* a vault unlock with no stored session (i.e.
arriving at Home with nothing to authenticate it) is explicitly left to the already-existing, already-built
expired-session machinery named in spec.md's own Edge Cases ("the existing expired-session handling —
established by F000, continued by RF07 — takes over exactly as it does elsewhere") — this unit does not add a
second mechanism for that.

## R11 — Reauth wiring reuses the established `reauthRequired` stream pattern

`SettingsBloc` exposes a broadcast `Stream<void> get reauthRequired`, fired whenever a repository call's single
silent-refresh retry (the same `_retryAfterSilentRefresh` shape `EntriesRepositoryImpl`/`ChatRepositoryImpl`
already use) still comes back `AuthExpiredFailure`. `SettingsPage` subscribes in `initState` and forwards to
`context.read<SessionBloc>().add(const AuthExpiredDetected())` — verbatim the same wiring `RecordsPage`/
`AppDrawer`/`ExportSheet` already each do for their own blocs (research.md precedent, RF06/RF07/RF05). The
already-wired, app-level `BlocListener<SessionBloc>` in `main.dart` is what actually raises the overlay; this
unit adds no second overlay-raising mechanism.

## R12 — Double-tap guards are in-flight booleans on `SettingsState`, not a separate mechanism

FR-022 is satisfied the same way `ExportBloc`'s own tap-guard already is: `isSigningOut`/`isDeletingAccount`
booleans on `SettingsState`, checked at the top of the corresponding event handler before any repository call
is made — a second tap while one is `true` is a no-op. No new synchronization primitive, no shared mutable
flag outside the bloc's own state.

## R13 — `AccountProfile`'s email-derived default is extracted from `AppDrawer`, not duplicated

`app_drawer.dart`'s `_displayNameFromEmail`/`_initialsFromEmail`/`_emailNameWords` (private, email-local-part
-splitting functions) carry their own comment: *"A real display name belongs to the Configurações unit... this
is a stand-in until that unit wires one in."* This unit is that unit. The three functions move, unchanged in
behavior, into `features/settings/domain/entities/account_profile.dart` as `AccountProfile`'s static
`defaultDisplayNameFromEmail(email)` and an `initials` getter (now deriving initials from whatever
`displayName` is actually showing — the cached/edited name once one exists, the email-derived default
otherwise — rather than always re-deriving from the email). `AppDrawer` is extended in place to read
`AccountProfileLocalCache.readDisplayName()` (falling back to the same default) instead of always showing the
email-derived stand-in, and to call the shared `AccountProfile.initials` instead of its own now-deleted private
copies — the drawer and Settings show the same name from the same source, by construction. This is a genuinely
cross-feature domain import (`features/home/presentation/` → `features/settings/domain/`), the same shape
`ChatBloc`'s import of `entries/domain/usecases/create_entry_usecase.dart` already establishes as acceptable
under Principle V.

## R14 — New design tokens: avatar size + chart geometry only; colors fully reused

`DesignTokens`' panel has no numeric bar-chart dimensions and no 52px avatar size (only `sizeAvatarMenu = 40`).
Four new, narrowly-scoped size tokens are added — `sizeAvatarSettings` (52, prototype-extract.md §6's own
"52px in Configurações"), `sizeChartBarMaxHeight`, `sizeChartBarWidth`, `sizeChartBarGap` — plus one new color,
`colorChartPlaceholder`, for the "light-gray placeholder chart icon" the zero-entries state needs (no existing
token is documented as light-gray; `colorBorder` (`#E1DACB`) is the closest existing neutral and is reused as
this new token's value rather than inventing an unrelated hex, keeping the palette internally consistent). The
"ochre" bar color is `DesignTokens.colorAccent` verbatim — already documented in the tokens panel and already
used for exactly this "CTA, insight, saved bookmark" register; the "10-bar ochre chart" wording in
prototype-extract.md §2.6 names the existing accent color, not a new one.

## R15 — RNF09's project-wide write-endpoint tally: this unit's contribution, not a final count

Every prior unit's plan reports its own new write-endpoint coverage without asserting the project-wide
fraction's exact final value (009's research.md R13 explicitly declines to, for the same reason — later units'
own contributions aren't yet verifiable from an earlier plan). This unit adds full timeout/malformed/
no-connection coverage for two **new** write endpoints — `account-delete` (`DELETE`, contracts/
account-deletion-repository.md) and `auth-logout` (`POST`, empty body, contracts/account-session-actions.md)
— and extends `account-settings-update`'s existing coverage (already contributed by RF03) with a second,
independently-sent field (`displayName`, contracts/account-profile-repository.md). `dashboard-aggregate-get`/
`dashboard-narrative-get` are `GET`s, outside RNF09's "write endpoint" tally, but are still fully
`Either`-typed and covered by contracts/dashboard-repository.md's own scenario table regardless, same as every
prior unit's read endpoints.

# Data Model: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard

Phase 1 output. Field names are this unit's own typed wrapper around `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s
`/dashboard/*`/`/account*`/`/auth/logout` schemas (research.md R1/R6/R7/R8/R9) — where this document and the
contract ever disagree, the contract prevails (Constitution Principle I).

## Domain entities (`lib/features/settings/domain/entities/`)

### `AggregateBucket`
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | `DateTime` | Parsed from the backend's `YYYY-MM-DD` string, date-only (no time component kept). |
| `count` | `int` | ≥ 0. |
| `sources` | `DashboardSourceCounts` | `{manual, audio, photo, chat}`, each `int` ≥ 0 — carried for completeness; this unit's chart only ever renders `count` (no per-source stacking/legend in scope). |

### `DashboardTotals`
`{count: int, sources: DashboardSourceCounts}` — the account-wide total for the requested period.

### `DashboardAggregate`
`{buckets: List<AggregateBucket>, totals: DashboardTotals}`. One pure extension method:
- `List<int> tenBars({DateTime? today})` → `research.md R2`'s `tenBars` function, `today` defaulting to
  `DateTime.now()` but overridable for deterministic tests.

### `DashboardNarrative`
`{text: String, generatedAt: DateTime}` — `generatedAt` is parsed but never displayed (spec.md: the
narrative's own content/quality is out of scope); kept only because the response always carries it and
dropping a required field silently would be a worse modeling choice than keeping it unused.

### `AccountProfile`
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `displayName` | `String` | 1–80 chars once set; the screen's single source of truth for both the name field and avatar initials. |
| `email` | `String` | Read-only in this unit (FR-009); sourced from `SessionRepository`'s already-resolved `Account.email`, never from a Settings-owned call. |

Static/instance helpers (research.md R13):
- `static String defaultDisplayNameFromEmail(String email)` — splits the email's local part on `._-`,
  title-cases each word, joins with a space (`"wagner.duarte@x.com"` → `"Wagner Duarte"`); `email` itself if
  the local part is empty.
- `String get initials` — 1–2 uppercase letters from `displayName`'s whitespace-split words (first letter of
  the first word, plus first letter of the second word if one exists); `"?"` if `displayName` is empty.
- `static bool isValidDisplayName(String value)` — `value.trim().isNotEmpty && value.trim().length <= 80`
  (FR-011) — pure, used by both the bloc (to block a bad submit client-side) and its own unit test.

## Repository interfaces (`lib/features/settings/domain/repositories/`)

### `DashboardRepository`
```dart
Future<Either<Failure, DashboardAggregate>> fetchAggregate();
Future<Either<Failure, DashboardNarrative>> fetchNarrative();
```
Both internally fixed to `period=all` (no parameter exposed, FR-002). Both retry exactly once via
`SessionRepository.refresh()` on `AuthExpiredFailure` (same shape as `EntriesRepositoryImpl`); a second
`AuthExpiredFailure` after that retry is returned as-is and triggers `SettingsBloc.reauthRequired`.

### `AccountProfileRepository`
```dart
Future<String?> readCachedDisplayName();                     // local-only, no network
Future<Either<Failure, String>> updateDisplayName(String name); // PATCH account-settings-update
Future<void> clearCachedDisplayName();                         // used by both Sair and Apagar conta
```
`updateDisplayName` persists the confirmed name into `AccountProfileLocalCache` before returning `Right` —
the local cache and "last confirmed backend value" are the same write, never two.

### `AccountDeletionRepository`
```dart
Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> deleteAccount(); // DELETE /account, confirmation: "DELETE" supplied internally
```

### Reused, unmodified, from other features (research.md R6/R8/R9)
- `BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save(bool)` (`vault/domain/`) — the network write.
- `VaultRepository.isBiometricPreferenceEnabled()` / `.setBiometricPreferenceLocally(bool)` /
  `.checkBiometricCapability()` / `.hasPinConfigured()` (`vault/domain/`) — local mirror + capability +
  post-logout destination.
- `AuthRepository.logout()` (`auth/domain/`, new method on an existing interface) — `POST /auth/logout`.
- `SessionRepository.clear()` (`session/domain/`) — wipes `SecureTokenStorage`.
- `EntriesRepository.clearLocalData()` / `ChatRepository.clearLocalData()` (new methods on existing
  interfaces) — wipe each feature's in-memory mirror + call its local cache's new `clear()`.

## Use cases (`lib/features/settings/domain/usecases/`)

### `SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`
`Future<Either<Failure, void>> call(bool enabled)` — research.md R6's await-then-mirror-or-revert sequence.
Depends on `BiometricsPreferenceRepository` + `VaultRepository` (both `vault/domain/`).

No other usecase classes are introduced — `DashboardRepository`/`AccountProfileRepository`/
`AccountDeletionRepository`'s methods are each already a single, narrow operation (the same "repository method
is usecase-shaped" choice `ExportBloc`/`ChatBloc` already make for most of their own calls); `SettingsBloc`
calls them directly.

## `SettingsState` (`lib/features/settings/presentation/bloc/settings_state.dart`, research.md R4)

One `Equatable` class, `copyWith` with the `RecordsLoaded`-style `_unset` sentinel for every nullable field
that must be explicitly clearable to `null`.

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dashboardStatus` | `DashboardStatus` enum: `loading, loaded, loadFailure` | `loading` | |
| `aggregate` | `DashboardAggregate?` | `null` | Set once `dashboardStatus == loaded`. |
| `dashboardFailure` | `Failure?` | `null` | Set once `dashboardStatus == loadFailure`; retryable per FR-007. |
| `narrativeStatus` | `NarrativeStatus` enum: `notRequested, loading, loaded, unavailable` | `notRequested` | `notRequested` for the zero/one-entry cases (FR-003/004); never transitions once there (FR-006's distinctness). |
| `narrativeText` | `String?` | `null` | Set once `narrativeStatus == loaded`. |
| `displayName` | `String` | `''` (loading placeholder) | The name actually shown — cached/edited value or the email-derived default once email is known. |
| `email` | `String` | `''` | From `SessionRepository`; read-only display. |
| `nameEditStatus` | `NameEditStatus` enum: `viewing, editing, saving, error` | `viewing` | |
| `nameDraft` | `String` | `''` | The in-progress edit field's text — preserved across a failed save (FR-012). |
| `nameEditFailureMessage` | `String?` | `null` | Validation (FR-011) or network (FR-012) message; cleared on re-entering edit mode. |
| `biometricToggleVisible` | `bool` | `false` | `true` only when `VaultRepository.checkBiometricCapability() == available` (FR-013's "hidden entirely" rule). |
| `biometricEnabled` | `bool` | `false` | Mirrors `VaultRepository.isBiometricPreferenceEnabled()` until a confirmed toggle changes it. |
| `biometricSaving` | `bool` | `false` | |
| `biometricFailureMessage` | `String?` | `null` | Set on a reverted save (FR-014); cleared on the next toggle attempt. |
| `isSigningOut` | `bool` | `false` | FR-022 guard. |
| `isDeletingAccount` | `bool` | `false` | FR-022 guard. |
| `deleteDialogOpen` | `bool` | `false` | Presentation-only flag the page uses to show/hide the confirmation dialog (FR-017/FR-021) — no backend call is implied by this alone. |
| `deleteFailureMessage` | `String?` | `null` | FR-020; shown inside the still-open dialog. |
| `signedOutDestination` | `SettingsDestination?` (`vault`/`login`) | `null` | A one-shot signal (research.md R10) — `SettingsPage`'s `BlocListener` navigates on any non-null value and the bloc never re-emits it after. |
| `accountDeletedDestination` | `SettingsDestination?` | `null` | Same shape as above, for the deletion success path — kept as a separate field from `signedOutDestination` only so a listener can tell which flow completed if ever needed for analytics/logging; both drive identical navigation. |

## Widgets and the tokens they consume (RNF08 — zero hardcoded values)

| Widget | New tokens used | Reused tokens |
|---|---|---|
| `ProfileHeader` (avatar + name + email) | `sizeAvatarSettings` (52) | `colorPrimary`, `colorOnPrimary`, `textTitleSm`, `textBodyMd`, `colorTextSecondary`, `spacingLg/Md` |
| `DashboardBarChart` (populated/one-bar states) | `sizeChartBarMaxHeight`, `sizeChartBarWidth`, `sizeChartBarGap` | `colorAccent` (ochre bars) |
| `DashboardEmptyState` (zero entries) | `colorChartPlaceholder` | `textBodyMd`, `colorTextSecondary` |
| `NarrativeView` (loaded / unavailable) | — | `textBodyMd`, `colorTextSecondary`, `colorError` |
| `BiometricToggleRow` | — | `textBodyLg`, `Switch` theme colors already derived from `AppTheme.theme` |
| `DeleteAccountDialog` | — | `colorError`, `textTitleLg`, `textBodyMd`, `radiusLg`, `elevation2` (same "confirmation dialog" component the session-expired overlay already uses) |

New `DesignTokens` additions (research.md R14), appended to the existing Sizes/Colors sections, values only:
`sizeAvatarSettings = 52`, `sizeChartBarMaxHeight = 120`, `sizeChartBarWidth = 20`, `sizeChartBarGap = 6`,
`colorChartPlaceholder = Color(0xFFE1DACB)` (= `colorBorder`'s own value, reused under a semantically distinct
name since the token panel's "placeholder chart icon" use is conceptually different from "dividers, borders"
even though the color is the same).

# Contract: `DashboardRepository`

`features/settings/domain/repositories/dashboard_repository.dart`, implemented by
`DashboardRepositoryImpl` (`features/settings/data/`), backed by `DashboardRemoteDataSource` calling
`dashboard-aggregate-get` (`GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=all`) and `dashboard-narrative-get`
(`GET /dashboard/narrative?period=all`).

```dart
abstract class DashboardRepository {
  Future<Either<Failure, DashboardAggregate>> fetchAggregate();
  Future<Either<Failure, DashboardNarrative>> fetchNarrative();
}
```

## Parsing

`fetchAggregate()` decodes `data.buckets[]` (`date`, `count`, `sources.{manual,audio,photo,chat}`) and
`data.totals` (`count`, `sources`) per `openapi.yaml`'s schema (both always present, even for a zero-entry
account — "always 200" per the contract's own summary line). `fetchNarrative()` decodes `data.text`/
`data.generatedAt`. A missing/mistyped required field on either call is a `ValidationFailure` (`TypeError`
caught, never thrown past this boundary — same pattern as `SessionRepositoryImpl._assembleFromCheckSession`).

## Retry-once-on-expiry

Both methods follow `EntriesRepositoryImpl._retryAfterSilentRefresh`'s exact shape: on `AuthExpiredFailure`,
call `SessionRepository.refresh()` once; on its own failure, return
`Left(AuthExpiredFailure(message: 'Session could not be renewed'))` (no second refresh attempt); on success,
retry the original call exactly once more and return whatever it resolves to.

## Scenario table (RNF09 — `fetchAggregate`/`fetchNarrative` are `GET`s, outside the write-endpoint tally,
but still fully `Either`-typed and tested)

| # | Scenario | Expected `Either` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 200, zero-entry account (`buckets: []`, `totals.count: 0`) | `Right(DashboardAggregate)` with an empty bucket list — never a `Left` |
| 2 | 200, well-formed non-empty payload | `Right(DashboardAggregate)` / `Right(DashboardNarrative)` |
| 3 | Dio timeout | `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` |
| 4 | No connection (no response) | `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` |
| 5 | 200 with a malformed body (`buckets` not a list / `count` missing) | `Left(ValidationFailure)` |
| 6 | 401 `AUTH_EXPIRED`, silent refresh succeeds | retried call's own result (success path re-exercises #1/#2) |
| 7 | 401 `AUTH_EXPIRED`, silent refresh itself fails | `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)`, and `SettingsBloc.reauthRequired` fires |
| 8 | `dashboard-narrative-get` returns `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | `Left(AiGenerationTimeoutFailure)` — mapped by `ErrorMapper` unchanged, surfaced by `SettingsBloc` as the "narrativa indisponível" state (FR-006), never conflated with #1's empty-history copy |

## `DashboardAggregate.tenBars()` — see data-model.md / research.md R2

Exercised directly by a domain unit test (no repository/network involved) for: empty input (10 zeros), a
single bucket on "today" (all weight in bar 9), buckets spanning exactly 10 days (one bucket per bar,
1:1), buckets spanning 100 days (several buckets folding into the same bar), and a bucket dated after `today`
(defensive — clamps to bar 9 rather than throwing or going out-of-range).
