# Contract: `AccountProfileRepository`

`features/settings/domain/repositories/account_profile_repository.dart`, implemented by
`AccountProfileRepositoryImpl` (`features/settings/data/`), backed by
`AccountSettingsRemoteDataSource.updateDisplayName()` (`PATCH account-settings-update`, body
`{"displayName": name}` only) and `AccountProfileLocalCache` (Keychain-backed, one key,
`flutter_secure_storage`, same pattern as `VaultSecureStorage`).

```dart
abstract class AccountProfileRepository {
  Future<String?> readCachedDisplayName();
  Future<Either<Failure, String>> updateDisplayName(String name);
  Future<void> clearCachedDisplayName();
}
```

## Behavior

- `readCachedDisplayName()` — local-only, no network, no `Either` (nothing here can fail in a way the caller
  must branch on beyond "was it ever set").
- `updateDisplayName(name)` — client-side validation (`AccountProfile.isValidDisplayName`) happens in
  `SettingsBloc` *before* this is called, per FR-011 ("no backend call is made"); this method itself always
  sends the request. On `Right`, the response's own `data.displayName` (not the caller's input string
  verbatim) is what gets written to `AccountProfileLocalCache` and returned — defensive against the backend
  ever normalizing the value (e.g. trimming), so the cache can never drift from what the server actually
  confirmed.
- `clearCachedDisplayName()` — deletes the one Keychain key; called by both the logout and account-deletion
  flows (research.md R9).

## Scenario table (RNF09 — `account-settings-update` is a write endpoint; this unit extends its existing
coverage, RF03 having already covered the `biometricEnabled`-only body shape)

| # | Scenario | Expected `Either` | Local cache after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 200, `displayName` 1–80 chars | `Right(name)` | Written |
| 2 | Dio timeout | `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` | Unchanged |
| 3 | No connection | `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` | Unchanged |
| 4 | 200 with a malformed body (`displayName` missing from the response) | `Left(ValidationFailure)` | Unchanged |
| 5 | 401 `AUTH_EXPIRED`, silent refresh succeeds | retried call's own result | per retried outcome |
| 6 | 401 `AUTH_EXPIRED`, silent refresh fails | `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)`, `reauthRequired` fires | Unchanged |

`SettingsBloc`'s own handling (not this repository's job) keeps `nameDraft`/edit mode intact on any `Left`
(FR-012) and returns the field to `viewing` mode showing the confirmed name only on a `Right`.

# Contract: `AccountDeletionRepository`

`features/settings/domain/repositories/account_deletion_repository.dart`, implemented by
`AccountDeletionRepositoryImpl` (`features/settings/data/`), backed by
`AccountDeletionRemoteDataSource` calling `account-delete` (`DELETE /account`).

```dart
abstract class AccountDeletionRepository {
  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> deleteAccount();
}
```

## Behavior

Always sends `{"confirmation": "DELETE"}` — the literal value the backend requires, supplied by the app
itself (FR-018); there is no caller-supplied parameter for it, so it is structurally impossible for this
method to ever send anything else. No retry-on-`AuthExpiredFailure` here: an expired session during the
delete-confirmation dialog is exactly spec.md's own Edge Case ("the session expires while Settings is open...
a confirmation dialog open") — the existing expired-session overlay takes over and the user re-authenticates
before retrying the tap, rather than this method silently refreshing and re-sending a destructive request
behind an overlay the user hasn't acknowledged yet. A plain `AuthExpiredFailure` `Left` surfaces through
`SettingsState.deleteFailureMessage` like any other failure and also fires `reauthRequired`.

## What `SettingsBloc` does around a `Right` result (research.md R9) — not this repository's job

On `Right(unit)`: `SessionRepository.clear()`, `AccountProfileLocalCache.clearCachedDisplayName()`,
`EntriesRepository.clearLocalData()`, `ChatRepository.clearLocalData()`, then resolve
`accountDeletedDestination` via `VaultRepository.hasPinConfigured()` (research.md R10). `VaultSecureStorage`'s
PIN hash and biometrics-preference mirror are deliberately **not** touched (research.md R9/R10).

## Scenario table (RNF09 — new write endpoint)

| # | Scenario | Expected `Either` | Account state after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 200 `{data: {ok: true}}` | `Right(unit)` | Backend account gone; app clears local state (above) |
| 2 | Dio timeout | `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` | Untouched — dialog shows retryable error (FR-020) |
| 3 | No connection | `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` | Untouched |
| 4 | 200 with a malformed body (`data.ok` missing/not `true`) | `Left(ValidationFailure)` | Untouched — never reports success on an ambiguous response |
| 5 | 401 `AUTH_EXPIRED` | `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)`, `reauthRequired` fires | Untouched |

## `SettingsBloc`'s own guard around this call (FR-022)

`isDeletingAccount` is checked and set to `true` before the call; a second `DeleteAccountConfirmed` event
while it is already `true` is dropped without calling this repository a second time (research.md R12) — same
shape as the `isSigningOut` guard around `AuthRepository.logout()`.

method to ever send anything else. No retry-on-`AuthExpiredFailure` here: an expired session during the
delete-confirmation dialog is exactly spec.md's own Edge Case ("the session expires while Settings is open...

before retrying the tap, rather than this method silently refreshing and re-sending a destructive request
behind an overlay the user hasn't acknowledged yet. A plain `AuthExpiredFailure` `Left` surfaces through
`SettingsState.deleteFailureMessage` like any other failure and also fires `reauthRequired`.

## What `SettingsBloc` does around a `Right` result (research.md R9) — not this repository's job

On `Right(unit)`: `SessionRepository.clear()`, `AccountProfileLocalCache.clearCachedDisplayName()`,
`EntriesRepository.clearLocalData()`, `ChatRepository.clearLocalData()`, then resolve
`accountDeletedDestination` via `VaultRepository.hasPinConfigured()` (research.md R10). `VaultSecureStorage`'s
PIN hash and biometrics-preference mirror are deliberately **not** touched (research.md R9/R10).

## Scenario table (RNF09 — new write endpoint)

| # | Scenario | Expected `Either` | Account state after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 200 `{data: {ok: true}}` | `Right(unit)` | Backend account gone; app clears local state (above) |
| 2 | Dio timeout | `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` | Untouched — dialog shows retryable error (FR-020) |
| 3 | No connection | `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` | Untouched |
| 4 | 200 with a malformed body (`data.ok` missing/not `true`) | `Left(ValidationFailure)` | Untouched — never reports success on an ambiguous response |
| 5 | 401 `AUTH_EXPIRED` | `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)`, `reauthRequired` fires | Untouched |

## `SettingsBloc`'s own guard around this call (FR-022)

`isDeletingAccount` is checked and set to `true` before the call; a second `DeleteAccountConfirmed` event
while it is already `true` is dropped without calling this repository a second time (research.md R12) — same
shape as the `isSigningOut` guard around `AuthRepository.logout()`.

# Contract: Sign-out (`AuthRepository.logout()` extension) + shared post-action destination

## `AuthRepository.logout()` — extends an existing interface (research.md R8)

`features/auth/domain/repositories/auth_repository.dart` gains one method, implemented by
`AuthRepositoryImpl` via a new `AuthRemoteDataSource.logout()` calling `auth-logout` (`POST /auth/logout`,
`bearerAuth`, empty body):

```dart
Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> logout();
```

`auth-logout`'s own response is `{data: {ok: true}}`; this method returns `Right(unit)` on 200 regardless of
the `ok` value's content (unlike `account-delete`, a non-`true` `ok` here is not treated as a malformed
response worth blocking on — FR-016 already says the local session is cleared "regardless of whether that
call succeeds or fails"). `AuthRepositoryImpl.logout()` does **not** call `SecureTokenStorage`/
`SessionRepository.clear()` itself — that stays `SettingsBloc`'s job (below), so `AuthRepository` keeps its
existing shape (it has never owned session-clearing; `AuthRepositoryImpl._persistOnSuccess` only ever writes,
never deletes).

## `SettingsBloc`'s sign-out sequence (FR-016)

```
on SignOutRequested, if isSigningOut: ignore (FR-022)
set isSigningOut = true
await authRepository.logout()        // result intentionally discarded either way
await sessionRepository.clear()
await accountProfileRepository.clearCachedDisplayName()
destination = hasPinConfigured() ? vault : login   // research.md R10
emit SettingsState(..., signedOutDestination: destination)
```
Note the `logout()` call's `Either` is awaited (so the request actually completes before local state is
wiped — avoiding a race where the app's own token is already gone when the request tries to attach it) but
never branched on; both `Left` and `Right` fall through to the same unconditional clear-and-navigate sequence
this is the one place in this unit's bloc logic where a `Left` is deliberately not surfaced as an error, per
FR-016's own explicit wording.

| # | Scenario | Local state after | Navigation |
|---|---|---|---|

| 2 | `logout()` → `Right`, no PIN configured (should not occur post-RF03, but not assumed impossible) | Session + cached name cleared | `AppRoutes.login` |
| 3 | `logout()` → `Left` (timeout/offline/`AUTH_EXPIRED`/malformed) | Session + cached name cleared regardless | Same as #1/#2 — failure never blocks the clear-and-leave sequence |
| 4 | A second `SignOutRequested` arrives while `isSigningOut == true` | No second `logout()` call (FR-022) | No second navigation |

`EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache` are **not** cleared on sign-out (research.md R9) — only
`AccountDeletionRepository`'s success path (contracts/account-deletion-repository.md) does that.

# Contract: `SettingsBloc`

`features/settings/presentation/bloc/`. A `get_it` `registerFactory` (screen-scoped, same lifetime pattern as
`RecordsBloc`/`ExportBloc` — a fresh instance per `AppRoutes.settings` visit, never a singleton, since
FR-008/FR-023 require a fresh fetch on every open rather than a resumed prior state).

## Dependencies

`DashboardRepository`, `AccountProfileRepository`, `AccountDeletionRepository`, `AuthRepository`,
`SessionRepository`, `SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`, `VaultRepository` — no `SessionBloc` import
(research.md R11 keeps that cross-bloc touch at the page, not the bloc, same as `RecordsBloc`).

## Events

| Event | Triggers |
|---|---|
| `SettingsOpened` | Dispatched once by the route builder (`app_router.dart`), mirroring `RecordsStarted`. Kicks off: aggregate fetch → (conditionally) narrative fetch; profile load (`SessionRepository`'s cached `Account.email` + `AccountProfileRepository.readCachedDisplayName()` or the email-derived default); biometric capability + current value. |
| `DashboardRetryRequested` | Re-runs the aggregate (and, if it then qualifies, narrative) fetch — FR-007's retry affordance. |
| `NameEditStarted` | `nameEditStatus → editing`, `nameDraft` seeded with the current `displayName`. |
| `NameDraftChanged(String value)` | Updates `nameDraft` only — no validation yet. |
| `NameEditCancelled` | `nameEditStatus → viewing`, `nameDraft` discarded. |
| `NameEditSubmitted` | Validates `nameDraft` first (FR-011); on failure, sets `nameEditFailureMessage`, stays `editing`, **no repository call**. On pass, calls `AccountProfileRepository.updateDisplayName`; on `Right`, `displayName` updates and `nameEditStatus → viewing`; on `Left`, stays `editing` with `nameDraft` intact and a retryable message (FR-012). |
| `BiometricToggleChanged(bool value)` | Optimistically flips `biometricEnabled` (RNF01), calls `SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`; reverts + message on `Left` (contracts/biometric-preference-settings-extension.md). |
| `SignOutRequested` | contracts/account-session-actions.md. |
| `DeleteAccountDialogOpened` / `DeleteAccountDialogCancelled` | Presentation-only — toggles `deleteDialogOpen`; cancel makes **no** backend call (FR-021). |
| `DeleteAccountConfirmed` | contracts/account-deletion-repository.md. |

## `reauthRequired` (research.md R11)

```dart
final _reauthController = StreamController<void>.broadcast();
Stream<void> get reauthRequired => _reauthController.stream;
```
Fired from inside any repository-call handler whenever the result is `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)` *after* that
repository's own single silent-refresh retry has already been exhausted (never for the first attempt, which
retries silently without surfacing anything) — same trigger condition `RecordsBloc`/`ChatSessionsBloc` already
use for their own `reauthRequired` streams. `close()` overridden to also close `_reauthController`, mirroring
`RecordsBloc`.

## `SettingsPage` wiring (`features/settings/presentation/pages/settings_page.dart`)

```dart
late final StreamSubscription<void> _reauthSubscription;

@override
void initState() {
  super.initState();
  _reauthSubscription = context.read<SettingsBloc>().reauthRequired.listen((_) {
    if (!mounted) return;
    context.read<SessionBloc>().add(const AuthExpiredDetected());
  });
}
```
A `BlocListener<SettingsBloc, SettingsState>` with `listenWhen` on `signedOutDestination`/
`accountDeletedDestination` becoming non-null performs the `context.go()` (research.md R10); a second
`BlocListener` (or the same one) shows the delete-confirmation `AlertDialog` while `deleteDialogOpen == true`,
closing it automatically on a successful deletion (the destination-change listener fires in the same frame).

## Session-expiry mid-screen (spec.md Edge Cases)

No special-cased event. The existing `main.dart`-level `BlocListener<SessionBloc>` raises the overlay exactly
as it does for every other screen; on re-authentication, `AppRoutes.settings`'s own route builder runs again
and dispatches a fresh `SettingsOpened` — the dashboard/profile/toggle are "reasonably re-requested, not
silently lost" (spec.md) by construction, not by any state this bloc preserves across the overlay itself.

## R16 — Post-reauth refresh on Settings: `RouteAware`, reusing the existing `chatRouteObserver`

Spec.md's Edge Case for Settings explicitly differs from Records'/Chat's own expired-session handling: "the
dashboard, profile, and any in-progress edit [are] reasonably re-requested, not silently lost" — "re-requested"
is a stronger guarantee than Records' own (which only promises no lost scroll position, not a refetch).
Because `showSessionExpiredOverlay` pushes the reauth `LoginSignupPage` via `rootNavigatorKey` — the exact
`Navigator` `GoRouter` itself renders into (`app_router.dart`'s own `navigatorKey: rootNavigatorKey`) — and
`context.push(AppRoutes.settings)` (how `AppDrawer` already reaches Settings) stacks `SettingsPage` on that
same navigator, the already-registered `chatRouteObserver` (`app_router.dart`, currently subscribed to only by
`HomeChatShellPage` to detect being covered) observes a Settings-covering reauth push/pop too. `SettingsPage`'s
`State` becomes `RouteAware`, subscribes to the same `chatRouteObserver` instance in `didChangeDependencies()`
(mirroring `HomeChatShellPage`'s own subscribe/unsubscribe shape exactly), and dispatches a fresh
`SettingsOpened` from `didPopNext()` — the moment the reauth page above it is popped and Settings becomes the
topmost route again. This is a second subscriber to an existing, already-general-purpose `RouteObserver`, not
a second observer registered on `GoRouter` itself.

# Contract: `SettingsBloc`

`features/settings/presentation/bloc/`. A `get_it` `registerFactory` (screen-scoped, same lifetime pattern as
`RecordsBloc`/`ExportBloc` — a fresh instance per `AppRoutes.settings` visit, never a singleton, since
FR-008/FR-023 require a fresh fetch on every open rather than a resumed prior state).

## Dependencies

`DashboardRepository`, `AccountProfileRepository`, `AccountDeletionRepository`, `AuthRepository`,
`SessionRepository`, `SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`, `VaultRepository` — no `SessionBloc` import
(research.md R11 keeps that cross-bloc touch at the page, not the bloc, same as `RecordsBloc`).

## Events

| Event | Triggers |
|---|---|
| `SettingsOpened` | Dispatched once by the route builder (`app_router.dart`), mirroring `RecordsStarted`. Kicks off: aggregate fetch → (conditionally) narrative fetch; profile load (`SessionRepository`'s cached `Account.email` + `AccountProfileRepository.readCachedDisplayName()` or the email-derived default); biometric capability + current value. |
| `DashboardRetryRequested` | Re-runs the aggregate (and, if it then qualifies, narrative) fetch — FR-007's retry affordance. |
| `NameEditStarted` | `nameEditStatus → editing`, `nameDraft` seeded with the current `displayName`. |
| `NameDraftChanged(String value)` | Updates `nameDraft` only — no validation yet. |
| `NameEditCancelled` | `nameEditStatus → viewing`, `nameDraft` discarded. |
| `NameEditSubmitted` | Validates `nameDraft` first (FR-011); on failure, sets `nameEditFailureMessage`, stays `editing`, **no repository call**. On pass, calls `AccountProfileRepository.updateDisplayName`; on `Right`, `displayName` updates and `nameEditStatus → viewing`; on `Left`, stays `editing` with `nameDraft` intact and a retryable message (FR-012). |
| `BiometricToggleChanged(bool value)` | Optimistically flips `biometricEnabled` (RNF01), calls `SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`; reverts + message on `Left` (contracts/biometric-preference-settings-extension.md). |
| `SignOutRequested` | contracts/account-session-actions.md. |
| `DeleteAccountDialogOpened` / `DeleteAccountDialogCancelled` | Presentation-only — toggles `deleteDialogOpen`; cancel makes **no** backend call (FR-021). |
| `DeleteAccountConfirmed` | contracts/account-deletion-repository.md. |

## `reauthRequired` (research.md R11)

```dart
final _reauthController = StreamController<void>.broadcast();
Stream<void> get reauthRequired => _reauthController.stream;
```
Fired from inside any repository-call handler whenever the result is `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)` *after* that
repository's own single silent-refresh retry has already been exhausted (never for the first attempt, which
retries silently without surfacing anything) — same trigger condition `RecordsBloc`/`ChatSessionsBloc` already
use for their own `reauthRequired` streams. `close()` overridden to also close `_reauthController`, mirroring
`RecordsBloc`.

## `SettingsPage` wiring (`features/settings/presentation/pages/settings_page.dart`)

```dart
late final StreamSubscription<void> _reauthSubscription;

@override
void initState() {
  super.initState();
  _reauthSubscription = context.read<SettingsBloc>().reauthRequired.listen((_) {
    if (!mounted) return;
    context.read<SessionBloc>().add(const AuthExpiredDetected());
  });
}
```
A `BlocListener<SettingsBloc, SettingsState>` with `listenWhen` on `signedOutDestination`/
`accountDeletedDestination` becoming non-null performs the `context.go()` (research.md R10); a second
`BlocListener` (or the same one) shows the delete-confirmation `AlertDialog` while `deleteDialogOpen == true`,
closing it automatically on a successful deletion (the destination-change listener fires in the same frame).

## Session-expiry mid-screen (spec.md Edge Cases)

No special-cased event. The existing `main.dart`-level `BlocListener<SessionBloc>` raises the overlay exactly
as it does for every other screen; on re-authentication, `AppRoutes.settings`'s own route builder runs again
and dispatches a fresh `SettingsOpened` — the dashboard/profile/toggle are "reasonably re-requested, not
silently lost" (spec.md) by construction, not by any state this bloc preserves across the overlay itself.

# Contract: `AppDrawer`'s display name (research.md R13) — extended in place, no behavior regression

`lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/app_drawer.dart` currently derives both the shown name and the
avatar's initials straight from the email (`_displayNameFromEmail`/`_initialsFromEmail`/`_emailNameWords`),
with a comment naming this unit as the one that wires in a real name. This unit:

1. Deletes `_displayNameFromEmail`/`_initialsFromEmail`/`_emailNameWords` from `app_drawer.dart`.
2. Adds `AccountProfile.defaultDisplayNameFromEmail`/`.initials` (data-model.md) to
   `features/settings/domain/entities/account_profile.dart`, carrying the exact same splitting/title-casing
   behavior forward byte-for-byte (same regex, same join) — not a rewrite, a relocation.
3. `_AppDrawerState` resolves its displayed name as:
   ```dart
   final cached = await getIt<AccountProfileLocalCache>().readDisplayName();
   final email = await getIt<SecureTokenStorage>().readAccountEmail();
   final displayName = cached ?? (email == null ? null : AccountProfile.defaultDisplayNameFromEmail(email));
   ```
   combined into one `Future<({String? displayName, String? email})>` (or two sequential `FutureBuilder`s —
   implementation detail left to tasks.md) so both pieces resolve before first paint, same as today's single
   `_accountEmail` future.
4. The avatar's `Text` child becomes `AccountProfile(displayName: displayName ?? '?', email: ...).initials`
   instead of the deleted `_initialsFromEmail(email)` call.

## Why this is safe to do here, not deferred

`AccountProfileLocalCache` is a new class this unit already creates (data-model.md); reading it from
`app_drawer.dart` is a presentation→data-layer-via-cache read no different in kind from `SecureTokenStorage`'s
own existing use in the same file — no new architectural seam, just one more secure-storage key read
alongside the one already there. Skipping this step would leave the drawer showing the stand-in email-derived
name forever even after a user successfully renames themselves in Settings — a visible inconsistency between
two screens showing what is supposed to be the same identity, directly contradicted by the comment this unit
is explicitly resolving.

## Test impact

`test/features/home/presentation/` (if any widget test already pumps `AppDrawer` against a fixed email) gains
one more stubbed dependency (`AccountProfileLocalCache.readDisplayName() → null`) to keep its existing
assertions about the email-derived fallback passing unchanged; no existing assertion's *expected value*
changes, since `null` cached ⇒ identical output to today's always-derive-from-email behavior.

# Quickstart: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard

Manual/exploratory validation guide — proves the feature end-to-end against a running backend. Automated
coverage (unit/bloc/widget) is tasks.md's job; this is the human-runnable complement, mirroring every prior
unit's quickstart shape (seeded accounts + a numbered walk-through per acceptance scenario).

## Prerequisites

- `.env` with `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` pointed at a reachable backend (Constitution Principle
  III) — same as every other unit's quickstart.
- `fvm flutter run` on an iOS simulator or device.
- At least these seeded test accounts (reuse whatever seeding mechanism prior units' quickstarts already
  established for `docs/input/backend/fixtures/`, extended with the counts this unit specifically needs):

| Account | Entries | Exercises |
|---|---|---|
| A | 0 | FR-003 (zero-entry dashboard state) |
| B | 1 | FR-004 (single-bar state) |
| C | 5 (all within the last 3 days) | FR-005/spec.md Clarification 1 (partial multi-bar chart, same-day-range degenerate bucketing) |
| D | 32, spread across several months | FR-005 (fully-populated 10-bar chart), acceptance scenario 3 |
| E | Any account with a configured PIN (post-RF03 first-time setup), biometrics available on the test device | User Story 3's biometric toggle |

## Story 1 — Dashboard

1. Log into **Account A**, open Settings (drawer → "Configurações"). Expect: light-gray placeholder chart
   icon, "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui," no narrative area at all.
2. Log into **Account B**. Expect: one small bar, "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.",
   no narrative area.
3. Log into **Account C**. Expect: the multi-bar chart with only some of the 10 bars populated (not the
   single-bar state), and a narrative paragraph once it resolves — confirms spec.md Clarification 1.
4. Log into **Account D**. Expect: all (or nearly all) 10 bars populated, ochre, plus a narrative paragraph.
5. From Account D, create one new entry on Home/Chat, return to Settings. Expect: the newly-created entry is
   reflected in the chart on this visit (FR-008) — not the pre-entry snapshot.
6. With the backend reachable, block only `dashboard-narrative-get` (e.g. a proxy rule, or temporarily
   renaming the function if testing against a local stack) while leaving `dashboard-aggregate-get` working, on
   Account D. Expect: chart renders correctly; narrative area shows "narrativa indisponível" wording, not a
   blank area and not Account A's empty-history copy (FR-006).
7. Block `dashboard-aggregate-get` itself (airplane mode, or a backend 500) on Account D. Expect: a distinct,
   retryable chart-area error state, no narrative requested, "Tentar novamente" (or equivalent) recovers once
   connectivity returns (FR-007).

## Story 2 — Account deletion

1. On any seeded account, tap "Apagar conta." Expect: centered dialog, red title "Apagar sua conta?",
   permanent/irreversible explanatory text, red "Apagar tudo," outline "Cancelar."
2. Tap "Cancelar." Expect: dialog closes; Settings unaffected; confirm via backend logs/dashboard that no
   `DELETE /account` request was sent.
3. Re-open the dialog, tap "Apagar tudo" with the backend reachable. Expect: lands at the vault/PIN screen (if
   this device has one configured) or login (if not); attempting to log back in with the same credentials
   fails (account gone).
4. Repeat with the backend unreachable (airplane mode). Expect: dialog stays open, shows a retryable error,
   account remains fully usable afterward (log back in to confirm).
5. Double-tap "Apagar tudo" quickly (airplane mode, so the first request hangs) — confirm via logs that only
   one `DELETE /account` request was ever sent (FR-022).

## Story 3 — Profile and sign-out

1. Open Settings. Expect: 52px initials avatar, current display name, email (read-only, no pencil/edit
   affordance next to it), pencil icon next to the name.
2. Tap the pencil. Expect: name becomes an editable field, pencil becomes a check, email unaffected.
3. Clear the field entirely and tap the check. Expect: inline validation error, field stays in edit mode, no
   network request (FR-011) — confirm via logs.

# Implementation Plan: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard

**Branch**: `011-settings-dashboard` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's
extension hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)

**Date**: 2026-10-24 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/011-settings-dashboard/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md`
§1 (RF09), §4 (RNF05), §6.6–6.7 (`dashboard-aggregate-get`/`dashboard-narrative-get`/`account-settings-update`/
`account-delete`), §6.1 (`auth-logout`), §8 (data model reference), §9 (stack), §13; `docs/input/backend/api/
openapi.yaml`'s `/dashboard/*`, `/account*`, `/auth/logout` schemas; `docs/input/backend/README.md`'s
function-name mapping; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`
§2.6, §6; and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on F000 (session, login, routing) and RF01 (entries
exist to aggregate), both already implemented. This is the unit that replaces `SettingsPlaceholderPage` (the
route `AppRoutes.settings` already points at a static "Ainda não disponível." placeholder) with the real
screen, and that finally wires in the real display name `app_drawer.dart`'s own stand-in email-derivation
comment has been waiting for since F000.

## Summary

The Settings screen (`AppRoutes.settings`, currently `SettingsPlaceholderPage`) becomes a real, four-concern
screen backed by one screen-scoped `SettingsBloc`: (1) an evolution dashboard — `GET /dashboard/aggregate` and
`GET /dashboard/narrative` as two independent calls, the aggregate's ten-bar chart built by a new pure
derivation (`DashboardAggregate.tenBars()`, research.md R2) and rendered with plain `Container`-based bars
(no new charting dependency, research.md R3); (2) an editable profile header (52px initials avatar, inline
pencil-to-check name editing via `PATCH /account/settings`, read-only email) backed by a new, narrow
`AccountProfileRepository` whose confirmed writes persist into a new `AccountProfileLocalCache`
(`features/settings/data/`, Keychain-backed) — the one local mirror this unit adds, since no earlier unit
ever wrote `displayName`; (3) a biometrics toggle that is hidden entirely on a device with no usable
capability and otherwise reuses RF03's own `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/`VaultRepository` as-is behind a
new, settings-owned, await-then-revert usecase (research.md R6) rather than RF03's deliberately
fire-and-forget one; (4) "Sair" (extends the existing `AuthRepository` with one new method, `logout()`) and
"Apagar conta" (a new `AccountDeletionRepository`, `DELETE /account`), both ending in the same
clear-local-state-and-navigate sequence spec.md's own Assumptions resolve to the existing vault/login routes
(research.md R10) — deletion alone additionally wipes `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache` (both extended in
place with a new `clear()` method) since "any other locally held user data" (FR-019) is a strictly wider
clear than logout's own FR-016 wording. `app_drawer.dart` is extended in place to read the same cached display
name (research.md R13), and `SettingsPage` becomes `RouteAware` on the already-existing `chatRouteObserver` so
re-authenticating mid-screen re-requests fresh data rather than only preserving stale state (research.md R15).

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from every prior
unit.

**Primary Dependencies**: None added. Reuses the full existing stack — `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`,
`equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, no new method needed — every call here is a plain JSON `call()`, the same
shape `BiometricsPreferenceRemoteDataSource` already uses), `flutter_secure_storage` (via a new
`AccountProfileLocalCache`, same pattern as `VaultSecureStorage`/`EntriesLocalCache`), `local_auth` (indirectly,
through the unmodified `VaultRepository`), `go_router` (no new route — `AppRoutes.settings` already exists;
only its builder changes); dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`. Research.md R3 explicitly rejects adding a
charting package — the 10-bar chart is plain `Container`s.

**Storage**: One new on-device key, `AccountProfileLocalCache`'s single `settingsDisplayName` Keychain entry
(research.md R5/R7) — the only new local persistence this unit introduces. `DashboardAggregate`/
`DashboardNarrative` are explicitly never persisted (FR-008 — "recomputed fresh... never served from a result
cached from a previous visit"), unlike `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`'s own cross-restart caches.

**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via `fvm flutter test
--coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now additionally exercising
`DashboardAggregate.tenBars()`'s pure bucketing (research.md R2 — the single richest piece of new domain
logic this unit adds, mirroring `DateRangeFilter`/`SyncBadgeState`'s existing pure-derivation test shape),
`AccountProfile.isValidDisplayName`/`.initials`/`.defaultDisplayNameFromEmail`, and
`SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`'s await-then-mirror-or-revert branches (contracts/
biometric-preference-settings-extension.md) against `mocktail` fakes of `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/
`VaultRepository` — no new fakes needed for `local_auth`/`flutter_secure_storage` themselves, since neither is
touched directly by anything new.

**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. No native project file touched; no new package needs an
iOS install step.

**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app. One new feature folder, `lib/features/settings/`
(domain/data/presentation, Principle V) replacing the one-file `SettingsPlaceholderPage` (deleted); three
existing files extended in place — `lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/auth_repository.dart` (+
`data`/`impl`, + `logout()`), `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` (+ `impl`, +
`clearLocalData()`), `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart` (+ `impl`, +
`clearLocalData()`) — plus their respective local caches (`EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`) each gaining a
new `clear()` method; `lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/app_drawer.dart` (display-name read, research.md
R13); `lib/core/routing/app_router.dart` (`AppRoutes.settings`'s builder); `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (5 new
tokens, research.md R14); `lib/core/di/service_locator.dart`. No backend/server code, no change to
`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`.

**Performance Goals**: RNF01 unchanged. The optimistic UI flips this unit adds — the biometric toggle's
immediate visual change before its network write resolves, and the name field's immediate return to display
mode is deliberately *not* optimistic (it waits for the `Right`, since a wrong optimistic name could be shown
then silently reverted, worse than a brief wait) — reflect within 100ms where used; every network call in
this unit's flow (dashboard load, name save, toggle save, sign-out, deletion) already has a loading indicator
by construction (`dashboardStatus == loading`, `nameEditStatus == saving`, `biometricSaving`, `isSigningOut`,
`isDeletingAccount` each drive one), satisfying the >300ms affordance requirement.

**Constraints**:
- No period-switching UI control (FR-002) — the dashboard always requests the fixed `period=all`.
- No AI persona selector or any other extension feature (FR-015) — `account-settings-update`'s `persona`
  field is never sent by this unit's requests and never read from its responses.
- No functionality belonging to a unit later than RF09 in the build order, and no backend/contract/config
  change (FR-024) — every endpoint this unit calls is one `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` already
  documents, called exactly as documented (contracts/*.md's own request-shape listings).
- Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature (Principle V) — `settings/domain/` imports only `equatable`/
  `fpdart`/`core/network/failure.dart`; `SettingsBloc` depends on `settings/domain/` repositories/usecases plus
  two other features' already-domain-layer interfaces (`vault/domain/`'s `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/
  `VaultRepository`, `auth/domain/`'s `AuthRepository`, `session/domain/`'s `SessionRepository`,
  `entries/domain/`'s `EntriesRepository`, `chat/domain/`'s `ChatRepository`) — never any other feature's
  `presentation/bloc/` (enforced by `test/architecture/no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`, unmodified, which
  already scans every `presentation/bloc/` path recursively).
- FR-022's concurrency guard is satisfied by `SettingsState`'s own `isSigningOut`/`isDeletingAccount` booleans
  (research.md R12), not a shared/persisted flag — the same shape `ExportBloc`'s own tap-guard already uses.
- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — the 5 genuinely
  new values this unit needs (data-model.md's token table, research.md R14) are added there, not inlined.

**Scale/Scope**: 1 new feature folder (`settings/`) with 4 domain entities + 1 pure bucketing extension, 3
repository interfaces + 1 reused usecase pattern (1 new settings-owned usecase), 3 data classes (2 remote data
sources + 1 local cache) + 3 repository impls, 1 bloc (+events/states), ~7 new presentation widgets; 3
existing features' interfaces each extended by exactly one method (+ impl); 2 existing local caches each
gaining a `clear()` method; 1 existing widget (`app_drawer.dart`) extended in place; 1 deleted file
(`settings_placeholder_page.dart`); 5 new `DesignTokens` values; ~14 new DI registrations.

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-checked after Phase 1 design — see bottom of this section.*

| Principle / Standard | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| I. Product Source of Truth | PASS | `docs/input/` read-only. Every technical-judgment decision this plan makes (R1–R16, research.md) is built directly on spec.md's own FRs/Clarifications/Assumptions/Edge-Cases wording — the data-flow split (R1), the bucketing arithmetic (R2), the no-new-dependency chart (R3), the flat composite state shape (R4), the per-field caching split (R5), the biometric await-revert usecase (R6), the narrow display-name repository (R7), the logout/deletion homing (R8), the clear-scope split (R9), the post-action destination (R10), the reauth-stream wiring (R11), the concurrency guards (R12), the extracted email-derivation (R13), the 5 new tokens (R14), the `RouteAware` post-reauth refresh (R15) — none reopens a resolved Clarification. |
| II. Fixed Technology Stack | PASS | No change to `flutter_bloc`/`fpdart`/`get_it`/Clean Architecture. Zero new dependencies (research.md R3) — the first unit in the delivery order to need no pubspec addition at all. |
| III. Backend Boundary | PASS | Only already-contracted functions called (`dashboard-aggregate-get`, `dashboard-narrative-get`, `account-settings-update`, `account-delete`, `auth-logout` — `docs/input/backend/README.md`'s own path→function table); no AI provider called directly (the narrative's Claude Haiku 4.5 generation stays entirely server-side, consumed only as the already-generated `text` field). `account-delete`'s `confirmation: "DELETE"` value is supplied by the app itself, never collected from the user as free text — no new surface for a credential/secret to leak through. |
| IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity | PASS | 5 new `DesignTokens` values (research.md R14/data-model.md), each traceable to either the prototype's own stated dimension (`sizeAvatarSettings = 52`, prototype-extract.md §6) or a reasonable, narrowly-scoped new value where the prototype's token panel is silent on chart geometry — never an inline literal in a widget file. UI text — "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui," "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.," "Apagar sua conta?," "Apagar tudo," "Cancelar," "Sair," "Apagar conta" — is exactly as spec.md's own FR/Acceptance-Scenario wording and prototype-extract.md §2.6 state it, in Portuguese; the one new copy this unit must author itself (the "narrativa indisponível" message's exact sentence, since the prototype names the state but not its literal string) is written in Portuguese consistent with the rest of the screen's register. |

Clean Architecture Folder Convention | PASS | `settings/domain/` imports only `equatable`/`fpdart`/`core/network/failure.dart` — confirmed against `domain_purity_test.dart` (unmodified, scans recursively). `SettingsBloc`'s dependency surface is exactly the repository/usecase interfaces listed in Technical Context's own Constraints entry — no other feature's `presentation/bloc/` import (confirmed against `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`, unmodified). |

## Complexity Tracking

| Addition | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
|---|---|---|
| A second, settings-owned biometric-save usecase (`SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`, research.md R6) alongside RF03's existing fire-and-forget one | FR-014 requires revert-on-failure; RF03's `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` deliberately never reports failure back to its caller — the two requirements are contradictory for the same repository call | Changing RF03's existing usecase's contract to support both modes (a flag/callback) — rejected: risks the already-shipped first-time-setup flow for a concern (Settings' revert UX) that first-time setup itself never needed |
| A new, settings-owned `AccountProfileLocalCache` rather than extending `VaultSecureStorage` with a `displayName` key | `displayName` has nothing to do with the vault/PIN domain `VaultSecureStorage` exists for; bolting an unrelated field onto it would blur that class's single responsibility for no benefit, since nothing about name caching needs anything `VaultSecureStorage` already provides | Adding a `displayName` key directly to `VaultSecureStorage` — rejected: couples two unrelated concerns (device-unlock secrets vs. a display preference) in one storage class, the same kind of bolt-on RF03's own `BiometricsPreferenceRepository` comment explicitly warns against ("rather than a general-purpose account-settings repository") |

*No entry needed beyond these three — the chart's no-new-dependency choice (R3) and the zero-new-Failure
-subtype outcome (every error code RF09's endpoints can return already exists in `failure.dart`) are each a
reduction in complexity, not an addition requiring justification.*

# Contract: `AppDrawer`'s display name (research.md R13) — extended in place, no behavior regression

`lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/app_drawer.dart` currently derives both the shown name and the
avatar's initials straight from the email (`_displayNameFromEmail`/`_initialsFromEmail`/`_emailNameWords`),
with a comment naming this unit as the one that wires in a real name. This unit:

1. Deletes `_displayNameFromEmail`/`_initialsFromEmail`/`_emailNameWords` from `app_drawer.dart`.
2. Adds `AccountProfile.defaultDisplayNameFromEmail`/`.initials` (data-model.md) to
   `features/settings/domain/entities/account_profile.dart`, carrying the exact same splitting/title-casing
   behavior forward byte-for-byte (same regex, same join) — not a rewrite, a relocation.
3. `_AppDrawerState` resolves its displayed name as:
   ```dart
   final cached = await getIt<AccountProfileLocalCache>().readDisplayName();
   final email = await getIt<SecureTokenStorage>().readAccountEmail();
   final displayName = cached ?? (email == null ? null : AccountProfile.defaultDisplayNameFromEmail(email));
   ```
   combined into one `Future<({String? displayName, String? email})>` (or two sequential `FutureBuilder`s —
   implementation detail left to tasks.md) so both pieces resolve before first paint, same as today's single
   `_accountEmail` future.
4. The avatar's `Text` child becomes `AccountProfile(displayName: displayName ?? '?', email: ...).initials`
   instead of the deleted `_initialsFromEmail(email)` call.

## Why this is safe to do here, not deferred

`AccountProfileLocalCache` is a new class this unit already creates (data-model.md); reading it from
`app_drawer.dart` is a presentation→data-layer-via-cache read no different in kind from `SecureTokenStorage`'s
own existing use in the same file — no new architectural seam, just one more secure-storage key read
alongside the one already there. Skipping this step would leave the drawer showing the stand-in email-derived
name forever even after a user successfully renames themselves in Settings — a visible inconsistency between
two screens showing what is supposed to be the same identity, directly contradicted by the comment this unit
is explicitly resolving.

## Test impact

`test/features/home/presentation/` (if any widget test already pumps `AppDrawer` against a fixed email) gains
one more stubbed dependency (`AccountProfileLocalCache.readDisplayName() → null`) to keep its existing
assertions about the email-derived fallback passing unchanged; no existing assertion's *expected value*
changes, since `null` cached ⇒ identical output to today's always-derive-from-email behavior.
